By participating, students gain valuable experience in applying mathematical concepts to real-world situations. The competition challenges students to think creatively and develop higher-order thinking skills essential for success in future endeavors.

Participants will have the opportunity to work with experienced mentors, gain valuable experience in entrepreneurship and innovation, and compete for prizes totaling over $10,000. The competition is a great way for students to develop their creativity, problem-solving skills, and teamwork abilities.

This competition introduces high school students to computer science principles while providing the opportunity to connect with other coders, learn from Google engineers, and hone coding abilities to win prizes.

Participants will master the technique of titration, a valuable analytical method used in various fields. Through hands-on experimentation, students will determine the concentration of unknown solutions, fostering their understanding of chemical reactions and the accurate measurement of substances. This competition provides a platform for students to showcase their analytical abilities, develop their problem-solving skills, and gain practical experience in a real-world laboratory setting.

This competition not only sparks a passion for science and innovation but also provides mentorship from experts in the field, fostering students' interests and preparing them for future careers in science and engineering.

title: US Brain Bee

By encouraging students to explore these fields, the Brain Bee fosters their curiosity and helps them make informed decisions about their future careers. Participation in this competition not only deepens students' understanding of the brain and its functions, but also nurtures their critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills, preparing them for success in higher education and beyond.

By participating in the competition, students can showcase their research, writing, and interpretation skills while engaging in creative and critical thinking. INSPIRE provides a platform for students to explore diverse perspectives, develop their understanding of complex issues, and communicate their findings to a wider audience. Participation in INSPIRE not only fosters students' intellectual growth but also enhances their academic profiles and prepares them for higher education and future careers.

Participants design and build bridges out of limited materials, fostering creativity, problem-solving, and teamwork. Building bridges helps students gain valuable hands-on experience in engineering principles, project management, and presentation techniques. By competing in this contest, students can develop their skills in a competitive setting, earn recognition for their achievements, and potentially secure internships or other opportunities at Brookhaven National Laboratory.

The competition ultimately aims to cultivate a passion for mathematics, preparing students for future academic and career pursuits.

Submissions will be judged by renowned National Geographic photographers and editors, providing participants with valuable feedback and recognition. Additionally, winning submissions will be published on the National Geographic website and social media platforms, giving students' work global exposure and inspiring future photographers to pursue their passion.

title: HPE CodeWars

By participating, students can sharpen their problem-solving and computational thinking skills, equipping themselves with a competitive edge for future endeavors. Through engaging challenges and team-based collaboration, CodeWars fosters creativity, innovation, and a passion for computer science, preparing students for success in the dynamic technological landscape that awaits them.

This program offers an exceptional platform for students to showcase their business acumen, innovative ideas, and leadership abilities. By participating in YouthBiz, students gain invaluable hands-on experience in developing and pitching their business plans to a panel of industry experts and investors. This challenging and rewarding experience not only fosters a deeper understanding of business principles but also helps students build confidence, cultivate critical thinking skills, and explore potential career paths in the business world.

The winning submissions will be announced through various channels, bringing recognition and admiration for the talented young artists who are committed to making a difference.

The competition provides a platform for students to showcase their passion for biology and collaborate with peers who share their interests.

Through their artistic submissions, participants can earn scholarships, recognition, and the opportunity to have their work featured in an exhibition. By using their imaginations and expressing their unique perspectives, students can not only inspire others but also deepen their own understanding of diversity and inclusion.

title: Physics Bowl
text: The Physics Bowl is a physics competition in the United States for high school students. It is sponsored by the American Association of Physics Teachers (AAPT), and the American Physical Society (APS). It is organized into 3 divisions: Division 1 is for 11th and 12th graders, Division 2 is for 9th and 10th graders and Division 3 is for younger students in grades 5-8. The questions cover a wide range of physics topics and are designed to test the students' problem-solving skills, critical thinking skills, and knowledge of physics. Participating in the Physics Bowl can help students to improve their problem-solving skills, critical thinking skills, and knowledge of physics.

title: Math Madness
text: Math Madness is a thrilling competition that allows high school students to showcase their mathematical prowess while honing their problem-solving, critical thinking, and teamwork skills. Open to students of all levels, this competition features a series of engaging challenges designed to stimulate mathematical curiosity and ignite a passion for the subject. By participating, students can connect with peers, test their limits, and gain invaluable experience that can prepare them for future endeavors in STEM fields and beyond.

title: Sony World Photography Awards
text: Calling all young high school photographers! Participate in the prestigious Sony World Photography Awards Youth Competition and showcase your talent to a global audience. The competition provides an unparalleled opportunity to gain recognition, connect with industry professionals, and inspire fellow creatives. Take your photography skills to the next level and submit your most compelling images to be judged by a panel of renowned experts. Embrace the challenge, showcase your artistic vision, and seize the opportunity to let your work shine on the world stage.

title: Creative Communication Contest
text: The Creative Communication Contest is an opportunity for high school students to showcase their writing skills and creativity. By submitting their poetry or essays, students have the chance to win prizes and recognition, as well as valuable feedback from a panel of experienced judges. Participation in the contest can help students develop their writing abilities, express their unique perspectives, and potentially earn recognition for their hard work and talent.

title: PLURAL+ Youth Video Festival
text: This competition encourages secondary school students to create compelling and thought-provoking videos that strive to promote diversity and inclusion. By participating, students have the extraordinary opportunity to develop their creative and technical skills, amplify their voices, and make a meaningful impact on fostering a more inclusive and understanding world.

title: American Mathematics Competitions
text: The American Mathematics Competitions (AMC) offer an exciting challenge for high school math students to test their skills and earn recognition. The AMC 10 and AMC 12 cater to 10th and 12th graders, respectively. Participation offers numerous benefits: it fosters problem-solving abilities, develops critical thinking, and enhances mathematical fluency. High-achieving students can earn prestigious awards, scholarships, and invitations to advanced math programs. The AMC provides a platform for students to excel and explore their passion for mathematics, setting them on a path to future success in STEM fields.

title: Patricia Grodd Poetry Prize
text: The Patricia Grodd Poetry Prize is a fantastic opportunity for high school poets to showcase their talents and earn recognition for their work. Winners of this prestigious competition will receive cash prizes and the esteemed honor of having their poems published in The Kenyon Review, a renowned literary magazine. This platform offers young poets a chance to gain exposure, build their portfolios, and connect with a wider audience.

title: National Science Bowl
text: The National Science Bowl is a thrilling buzzer-style tournament that engages high school students in a game of general science trivia covering core sciences, math, computer science, and logic. Participating in the competition fosters academic prowess, inspires teamwork, and nurtures a passion for STEM subjects. Winning teams have the opportunity to advance to national competitions, showcasing their knowledge and earning prestigious recognition.

title: Science Olympiad
text: Science Olympiad offers a unique platform for high school students to engage in collaborative problem-solving, fostering critical thinking, teamwork, and communication skills. By participating in diverse scientific events, students deepen their understanding of STEM principles, enhance their research abilities, and develop leadership qualities. Science Olympiad empowers students to explore their scientific passions, preparing them for future careers in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).

title: Boston University Summer Term RISE Internship/Practicum
text: Participate in the Boston University's Research in Science & Engineering (RISE) high school summer program for an immersive experience in research and scientific discovery. Under the guidance of renowned scientists, students will engage in hands-on research projects, advancing their knowledge and skills in STEM fields. The six-week program offers an exceptional opportunity to explore academic interests, build professional networks, and gain valuable practical experience at a top research university.

title: NASA
text: NASA's internship program offers high school students hands-on research and operational experiences at NASA facilities. Mentored by a NASA professional, students engage with NASA's missions, contribute to operations, and gain invaluable practical experience in science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) fields. This prestigious program fosters students' interest in STEM careers, preparing them for leadership roles in future space exploration and scientific advancements.

title: Princeton Plasma Physics Lab Summer Internship Program
text: The Princeton Plasma Physics Lab Summer Internship Program offers high school seniors the opportunity to work on a project with a member of PPL's research or engineering staff. Interns will gain hands-on experience in a variety of scientific disciplines, including plasma physics, astrophysics, and nuclear engineering. They will also have the chance to learn about the latest advances in these fields and to network with leading scientists and engineers. In addition to the academic benefits, interns will also receive a stipend and have the opportunity to participate in a variety of social and cultural activities. The program is highly competitive, but it is an excellent opportunity for high school seniors who are interested in pursuing a career in science or engineering.

title: Astronomy and Astrophysics Olympiad
text: The United States Astronomy and Astrophysics Olympiad (USAAAO) is a competitive examination-style contest for high school students with a passion for astronomy and astrophysics. The top performers from this national competition qualify to represent the United States at the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics (IOAA). Participation in the USAAAO provides students with an exceptional opportunity to challenge their knowledge, engage with like-minded peers, and potentially earn recognition for their academic excellence on the global stage.

title: Research Science Institute (RSI)
text: The Research Science Institute (RSI) is a highly selective summer program for high school students with a passion for science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). Each year, 80 of the world's most accomplished high school students gather at MIT for an immersive experience that combines rigorous coursework in scientific theory with hands-on research in cutting-edge fields. Through RSI, students gain invaluable experience in research methodology, critical thinking, and problem-solving, while also building a network of peers and mentors. Participation in RSI opens doors to future opportunities in STEM careers and provides a transformative experience that fosters intellectual growth and scientific curiosity.

title: Simons Summer Research Program
text: The Simons Summer Research Program is a highly selective opportunity for academically advanced high school juniors who seek to engage in hands-on research in STEM fields. This program offers exceptional students the chance to collaborate with renowned faculty mentors at Stony Brook University, participate in active research teams, and immerse themselves in a dynamic research environment. Through this program, students gain valuable laboratory experience, develop essential scientific skills, and contribute meaningfully to ongoing research projects. The program provides an unparalleled opportunity to experience the rigors and rewards of scientific inquiry, while fostering connections within the STEM community and nurturing students' passion for research.

title: Summer Science Program (SSP)
text: The Summer Science Program (SSP) provides an exceptional experience for high school students passionate about science. Participants immerse themselves in hands-on experimentation, working in teams to conduct authentic research projects. Through data collection and analysis, they gain a profound understanding of scientific principles. Beyond scientific skills, SSP fosters teamwork, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities essential for success in STEM fields. Graduates join a global network of over 2,500 alumni, connecting with like-minded individuals and unlocking opportunities for further scientific exploration.

title: Texas Tech University - The Clark Scholars Program
text: The Anson L. Clark Scholar Program is an enriching seven-week summer research experience for high school juniors and seniors. This intensive program brings together twelve highly qualified students from diverse backgrounds to engage in cutting-edge research under the guidance of esteemed Texas Tech University faculty. Throughout the program, participants gain invaluable hands-on research skills, attend workshops and seminars, and collaborate with peers who share their passion for learning. Additionally, they receive a $1000 stipend for their participation, making this an exceptional opportunity for ambitious high school students seeking an immersive research experience.

title: Michigan State University - High School Honors Science, Math and Engineering Program (HSHSP)
text: This longstanding summer research program at Michigan State University grants motivated high school students rare opportunities to engage in deep, focused research experiences alongside leading scientists and engineers in advanced university research laboratories. Students will live on campus, conduct groundbreaking research projects, and participate in science and technology lectures and field trips.

title: University of Florida - Student Science Training Program (SSTP)
text:
The University of Florida Student Science Training Program (SSTP) is a six-week residential summer program for talented high school seniors interested in science, medicine, or engineering careers. Participants work with University of Florida faculty mentors as part of collaborative research projects in disciplines ranging from computer science to medicine and engineering. Student benefits include:
>**Hands-on research experience:** Conduct original research alongside distinguished UF faculty in state-of-the-art facilities.
>**Expert mentorship:** Build relationships with UF faculty and graduate researchers who will guide and support your academic and career development.
>**Immersive learning environment:** Join a vibrant undergraduate research community and participate in seminars, workshops, and field trips that expand your knowledge beyond the lab.
> **Professional development:** Enhance your resume with hands-on research experience and develop valuable science communication and collaborative research skills.
>**Career exploration:** Get first-hand insights into a wide range of STEM careers and make informed decisions about your future.

title: MIT Introduction to Technology, Engineering, and Science
text: MITES (formerly OEOP) empowers highly motivated 7th-12th grade students from diverse backgrounds to pursue STEM careers. Through transformative summer programs, MITES builds confidence, fosters community, and provides a solid foundation in technology, engineering, and science. Participation is free for all, ensuring equitable access to STEM education for underrepresented students. By investing in the next generation of STEM leaders, MITES aims to advance equity and create a brighter future for all.

title: Summer Academy for Math and Science
text: The Summer Academy for Math and Science (SAMS) is a 6-week residential academic program for exceptional high school students hosted by Carnegie Mellon University. As SAMS Scholars, students engage with world-renowned faculty and skilled staff mentors. The program provides a deeper understanding of STEM via traditional classroom instruction, hands-on projects, and sustained engagement. Students collaborate and connect with peers from across the country while developing problem-solving skills, critical thinking, and communication abilities. SAMS not only enriches students' academic experiences but also fosters their personal and professional growth.

title: USC Summer High School Intensive in Next-Generation Engineering (SHINE)
text: USC Viterbi's Summer High School Intensive in Next-Generation Engineering (SHINE) is a unique opportunity for high school students to immerse themselves in cutting-edge engineering research at a top-ranked university. Through hands-on experiences in various fields such as biomedicine, robotics, and aerospace, students will gain firsthand insights into how engineering tackles real-world problems. By joining a USC Viterbi professor's research team for seven weeks, participants will develop essential skills and knowledge that can enhance their STEM education and future career paths.

title: Clean Tech Competition
text: The Clean Tech Competition is an opportunity for pre-college youth to engage in STEM-related research and design challenges. Each year, the competition focuses on a different issue related to environmentally responsible energy sources. The goal of the competition is to foster a deeper understanding of STEM concepts, recognize outstanding talent, and prepare the next generation of innovators. Students who participate in the Clean Tech Competition develop valuable skills in research, design, problem-solving, and communication. They also have the opportunity to work with mentors from leading universities and research institutions. The Clean Tech Competition is a great way for students to explore their interests in STEM, develop their skills, and gain experience in research and design.

title: Clarks Scholars Texas Tech
text: The Anson L. Clark Scholar Program at Texas Tech University is a seven-week summer research program designed for highly qualified high school juniors and seniors. This intensive program provides Scholars with the opportunity to conduct hands-on research under the mentorship of experienced faculty, gaining valuable experience in STEM fields. Participation in the Clark Scholar Program not only enhances Scholars' research skills and knowledge, but also helps them develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication abilities. It also exposes Scholars to the university environment and research opportunities, fostering their interest in pursuing higher education and STEM careers.

title: Aspiring Scientists Summer Internship Program (ASSIP)
text: Aspiring high school scientists are highly encouraged to apply for this nationally recognized, transformative summer internship program. ASSIP pairs high school and undergraduate students with faculty researchers at George Mason University and collaborating institutions, These students work one-on-one with their faculty mentors on research projects that use the latest technology. Through this program, students will gain hands-on research experience, access to state-of-the-art facilities, develop critical thinking skills, and grow as scientists.

title: Samsung Solve for Tomorrow
text: Samsung Solve for Tomorrow is an annual competition that challenges high school students to use STEM to solve real-world problems in their communities. Students can compete for up to $100,000 in prizes for their school, as well as the opportunity to work with Samsung employees to develop their prototypes. The competition is open to all public schools grades 6-12, and applications are due in February of each year.

title: ArcGIS Online Competition for US High School & Middle School Students
text: If you are a high school student in the US, participate in Esri's 2022 ArcGIS Online Competition and use ArcGIS software to demonstrate your learning to an authentic audience. You could have your GIS work, or that of your team, featured on Esri's website and win other high-tech prizes by creating and sharing a map, story, or app about your home state.

title: Plant the Moon Challenge
text: The Plant the Moon Challenge is a global science experiment and research challenge for high school students. Participants will join a global team to examine how vegetable crops can grow in lunar or Martian soil. Each team will receive real soil simulant from the University of Central Florida’s CLASS Exolith Lab. Students will design and conduct a set of experiments using this simulant to grow crops for a future long-duration mission. The Plant the Moon Challenge is a great opportunity for students to learn about space exploration, plant science, and research. It is also a chance to win prizes and recognition for their work.

title: AFA StellarXplorers National Space Design Competition
text: The StellarXplorers National Space Design Competition is a fun and educational team-building competition where students in grades 9-12 can solve real-world space system design challenges. Participants work in teams to plan orbits, select satellite components, and choose launch vehicles, all while learning about the latest advances in space technology. The competition is a great way for students to develop their problem-solving, critical thinking, and teamwork skills, while also gaining valuable experience in the field of space exploration. Past participants have gone on to pursue careers in aerospace engineering, astrophysics, and other STEM fields.

title: Battle of the Brains
text: Burns & McDonnell Battle of the Brains, an exciting STEM competition for K-12 students, offers high schoolers a remarkable opportunity to showcase their creativity and ingenuity. Teams conceptualize an interactive exhibit for Science City's hands-on science museum, gaining invaluable experience in design, engineering, and communication. By participating, high school students not only compete for a share of $155,000 in STEM education grants for their schools, but also contribute to the creation of a lasting legacy at one of Kansas City's top educational attractions.

title: Junior Science and Humanities Symposium
text: The JSHS fosters a passion for STEM among high school students by providing a platform to showcase their original research through rigorous competition. Participation in this esteemed symposium not only challenges students intellectually but also cultivates their research skills, confidence, and critical thinking abilities. Winners are awarded prestigious scholarships and recognition, while all participants benefit from engaging workshops, interactive panel discussions, and unrivaled networking opportunities within the STEM community.

title: Phoenix Space LaunchPad Challenge
text: Calling all high school space enthusiasts! The Phoenix Space LaunchPad Challenge invites you to showcase your scientific prowess and creativity. Engage in a global competition designed to foster innovation, problem-solving, teamwork, and presentation skills in the realm of space science. Immerse yourself in cutting-edge research, connect with fellow space enthusiasts, and elevate your scientific horizons by participating in this prestigious competition.

title: Regeneron Science Talent Search (STS)
text: The Regeneron Science Talent Search (STS) is a nationwide competition that honors and supports the most talented young scientists in the United States. Each year, nearly 1,900 high school seniors submit original research in critically important scientific fields of study. The top 40 students are invited to participate in a week-long competition in Washington, D.C., where they present their work to a panel of judges and compete for scholarships and other awards. Participating in the STS offers high school students an unparalleled opportunity to showcase their research skills, gain mentorship from leading scientists, and connect with a community of like-minded individuals. The competition also provides a platform for students to share their passion for science and inspire future generations of scientists.

title: Stockholm Junior Water Prize
text: The Stockholm Junior Water Prize is an international competition that encourages high school students to conduct water-related science projects and fosters their interest in water and sustainability issues. Participating in this competition provides numerous benefits for students, including the opportunity to develop their problem-solving and critical thinking skills, gain hands-on research experience, and expand their knowledge of water-related topics. The competition also recognizes and rewards outstanding student projects, showcasing their scientific abilities and fostering their passion for water-related careers.

title: The Earth Prize
text: The Earth Prize is an annual competition for students aged 13-19 that rewards projects with the most potential to address environmental issues. The $200,000 grand prize is split among the winning team members, providing financial support for their continued education and environmental endeavors. Participation in the competition fosters critical thinking, problem-solving, and research skills, while also raising awareness about pressing environmental concerns. By empowering young minds to develop innovative solutions, The Earth Prize cultivates future leaders in the field of environmental sustainability.

title: National Science Bee
text: For high school aged students, the National Science Bee presents a prime opportunity to challenge their scientific aptitude through a nationally renowned competition. Participation affords young scholars the chance to showcase their in-depth comprehension across diverse scientific disciplines, engage with peers of similar scientific interests, and acquire valuable critical thinking skills essential for future academic and professional endeavors in the STEM field. Beyond the thrill of competition, the Bee empowers students with confidence in their scientific abilities and cultivates a passion for lifelong scientific exploration.

title: UC Santa Barbara Research Mentorship Program (RMP)
text: The Research Mentorship Program at UC Santa Barbara is a prestigious summer program that provides gifted high school students with an unparalleled opportunity to conduct university-level research alongside accomplished mentors. Through this competitive six-week program, participants gain hands-on experience in a wide range of disciplines, developing valuable research skills, critical thinking abilities, and connections within the academic community. The program offers a transformative experience for aspiring STEM professionals, equipping them with the knowledge and confidence to excel in their future endeavors.

title: Raleigh Residential Camps
text: This is an excellent opportunity for high school students to experience an actual field of engineering and get a glance of future college life while living on the NC State campus. The in-person residential program offers students the prospect of understanding college life, exploring a specific branch of engineering through coursework and activities, living in actual on-campus housing, and socializing with like-minded peers. Participation in this summer program will provide high school students with a hands-on experience and an in-depth understanding of the field of engineering they are interested in.

title: Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Scholars Program
text: The AFRL Scholars Program provides top high school students with the chance to gain invaluable hands-on research experience under the guidance of experienced scientists and engineers. Through this program, students contribute to meaningful projects, develop their STEM skills, and gain insights into potential career paths in research and development. Participating in this program provides a competitive edge in college applications and future career endeavors.

title: Princeton Laboratory Learning Program
text: Participation in the Laboratory Learning Program provides high school students with an unparalleled hands-on research experience. Working alongside Princeton faculty and research staff, students are immersed in ongoing research projects, gaining a deep understanding of the scientific process and cutting-edge advancements in their chosen fields. The program fosters intellectual curiosity, develops critical thinking skills, and empowers students to explore their passion for STEM.

title: Johns Hopkins Engineering Innovation Pre-College Programs
text: The Johns Hopkins Engineering Innovation Pre-College Programs provide students with an unparalleled opportunity to explore the world of engineering through hands-on projects and immersive experiences. Participants can choose from three exciting tracks: designing devices to enhance well-being, improving wind energy efficiency, or designing spaghetti bridges with exceptional strength. The program fosters creativity, collaboration, and critical thinking, all while offering the chance to earn college credit. Whether students participate on-campus or online, they will gain valuable insights into engineering principles and the opportunity to connect with like-minded peers from around the globe.

title: MIT THINK Scholars Program
text: The MIT THINK Scholars Program is a unique opportunity for high school students interested in research to receive guidance and support in the early stages of their projects. Unlike many research programs that require prior experience, THINK welcomes students with strong background knowledge who are eager to develop their research skills. Participants will benefit from mentorship, workshops, and access to MIT resources, empowering them to refine their research ideas, design experiments, and prepare for future research endeavors.

title: Space Settlement Design Competition
text: The Space Settlement Design Competition immerses students in the thrilling realm of space exploration and design. By collaborating in teams, participants delve into the complexities of space settlement, crafting comprehensive proposals that emulate the real-world challenges faced by aerospace industry professionals. This invaluable experience nurtures students' creativity, analytical skills, and problem-solving abilities, preparing them for future endeavors in STEM fields. The competition fosters a shared passion for space exploration, igniting a thirst for knowledge and innovation that will shape the next generation of space pioneers.

title: spUN Debate Program of the National Space Society
text: High school students with a passion for space and leadership should consider participating in the NSS's space policy and UNiversalization (spUN) Debates program. This program provides an opportunity for students to engage in debates on cutting-edge space policy issues and develop their public speaking, critical thinking, and leadership skills. The program is open to students of all grades and backgrounds, and participants will have the chance to interact with experts in the field of space exploration.

title: Gerard K. O'Neill Space Settlement Contest
text: This annual contest invites high school students to design and showcase their innovative ideas for orbital space habitats. Participation offers a unique opportunity for students to engage in STEM fields, foster critical thinking skills, and explore potential career paths in space exploration. The contest empowers them to envision and create sustainable solutions for human habitation beyond Earth, inspiring their scientific curiosity and interest in space-related studies.

title: NASA Cinespace Short Film Competition
text: The NASA Cinespace Short Film Competition offers high school students a unique opportunity to showcase their creativity by creating short films inspired by NASA's vast digital archives. Participation in the competition provides students with a platform to display their talent and enthusiasm for astronomy and filmmaking. It also allows them to collaborate with NASA scientists, gaining invaluable insights into the field of space exploration. By submitting their films, students have the chance to win cash prizes, earn recognition from renowned director Richard Linklater, and have their work screened at the prestigious Houston Cinema Arts Festival in November. Whether they are aspiring filmmakers or enthusiastic science enthusiasts, this competition presents a compelling opportunity for high school students to explore their passions and share their vision with the world.

title: NASA Langley Student Art Contest
text: This contest offers a unique opportunity for high school students to showcase their artistic talents while exploring the world of science, aeronautics, and exploration. Participation in the competition encourages the development of creativity, critical thinking skills, and a passion for STEM subjects. By submitting their artwork, students not only express their unique perspectives and interpretations but also have the potential to earn recognition and prizes.

title: Perry Research Scholars Institute
text: The Perry Research Scholars Institute (PRSI) offers high school students a unique opportunity to delve into the world of academic research at the University of Iowa. During the two-week residential program, students engage with distinguished researchers from diverse fields, including anthropology, business, education, engineering, and medicine. Through classroom discussions, guest lectures, and research facility tours, participants gain firsthand insights into the research process, cutting-edge technologies, and career paths of leading scholars. The experience fosters critical thinking, problem-solving, and a passion for knowledge, while providing valuable connections with experts in their fields.

title: C-Tech² - Computers and Technology at Virginia Tech
text: C-Tech² is a program designed to introduce promising high school girls to the world of college life and STEM fields. Throughout the program, participants will learn about various aspects of college, including residence halls, classrooms, and academic resources. Additionally, they will have the opportunity to engage with professors, researchers, and current students, gaining insights into cutting-edge technologies and career paths in STEM. By participating in C-Tech², students can not only broaden their horizons but also gain valuable knowledge and skills that will prepare them for success in college and beyond.

title: UPenn Engineering Summer Academy
text: The Engineering Summer Academy at Penn (ESAP) provides high school students with an immersive and challenging learning experience in engineering. Through the Summer Academy in Applied Science and Technology (SAAST), students engage in cutting-edge research and hands-on projects, guided by renowned faculty and researchers. This program empowers students to explore their interests in STEM, develop problem-solving skills, and gain a competitive edge in the field of engineering.

title: Frontiers of Science Institute
text: The Frontiers of Science Institute (FSI) at the University of Northern Colorado (UNC) offers a six-week summer program for high school students. The program introduces new scientific concepts beyond the high school curriculum through field trips, industrial visitations, and seminars led by professionals from academia and industry. Students also engage in hands-on laboratory activities. By participating in FSI, high school students can gain valuable insights into STEM fields, explore career opportunities, and enhance their scientific knowledge and skills.

title: Columbia Summer High School Academic Program for Engineers
text: Columbia Engineering's Summer High School Academic Program for Engineers (SHAPE) is a selective program for high school students with an aptitude for STEM: science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. The program offers college-level, project-based courses in engineering and provides students with an immersive experience in engineering education. Through access to prestigious faculty, peers, and industry partners, students will learn about cutting-edge engineering concepts, develop problem-solving and critical-thinking skills, and explore possible engineering disciplines. The program also includes site visits and workshops to supplement hands-on learning opportunities. Participating in SHAPE can help students solidify their aspirations in STEM, prepare for college engineering programs, and connect with like-minded individuals.

title: The CalcuLIT Club
text: The CalcuLIT Club is a lively math club that high school students passionate about calculus and mathematics can join. The club meets weekly virtually to discuss, learn, and study the fascinating world of calculus. Gaining recognition as an intellectual and creative hub, the CalcuLIT Club has attracted members ranging from high schoolers to math teachers and welcomes new members. Whether you are an expert or new to calculus, you are invited to join. Come explore the powers of mathematics as part of the CalcuLIT Club.

title: HOSA
text: HOSA-Future Health Professionals is a student-led organization that emphasizes engagement in the health industry. It provides opportunities for high school students to explore healthcare careers through hands-on competitions that enhance their abilities in leadership, teamwork and critical thinking. Participation in HOSA competitions provides practical experience, fosters professional development, and prepares students for success in the healthcare field.

title: Scripps Translational Science Institute Student Research Internship Program
text: This competitive research internship program provides highly motivated high school students with an unparalleled opportunity to delve into genomics and genetic studies. Guided by renowned scientists at the Scripps Translational Science Institute, interns gain invaluable hands-on experience in biomedical research. Through personalized mentorship and collaborative laboratory work, they develop comprehensive research projects and present their findings, fostering their scientific inquiry and critical thinking skills. This intensive program nurtures future science leaders by exposing them to cutting-edge technology and methodologies while fostering their passion for scientific exploration.

title: Harvard CURE Program
text: The Harvard CURE Program offers an unparalleled opportunity for high school students with a passion for science to engage in cutting-edge cancer research under the guidance of esteemed mentors at Harvard Medical School. By joining this program, students gain invaluable hands-on experience, develop their scientific knowledge and skills, and acquire marketable expertise that will enhance their future careers in the biomedical sciences. Participants also receive comprehensive career development support, including guidance on college applications, research projects, and professional development opportunities.

title: Rockefeller University Summer Science Research Program
text: Join the prestigious Rockefeller University Summer Science Research Program and immerse yourself in the world of biomedical research! This exclusive program, for juniors and seniors, offers an unparalleled opportunity to engage in cutting-edge research alongside expert scientists. Spend seven weeks conducting lab experiments, participating in vibrant coursework, and expanding your knowledge through interactive lectures. Gain hands-on research experience, enhance your critical thinking skills, and discover potential career paths in the field of science while enjoying the comfort of provided room and board.

title: Aspirnaut Summer Research Internships for High School Students
text: Aspirnaut Summer Research Internships provide high school students with a transformative opportunity to delve into the world of STEM research at Vanderbilt University. These paid internships offer hands-on laboratory experiences in biomedical research, led by expert mentors. Interns reside on campus for six weeks, enhancing their understanding of scientific principles while honing their research skills. The program equips students with valuable insights into academic and research careers, fostering their passion for STEM and empowering them with a solid foundation for future success.

title: Coriell Institute for Medical Research Summer Internships
text: The Coriell Institute for Medical Research annually offers  a selective summer experience to motivate students interested in STEM fields through an all expenses paid immersive four  week program occurring annually in July. High students who are able to participate in the entire four-week period are invited to apply for one of the coveted few slots in the program, which provides an unparalleled glimpse into the inner-workings of a world-renowned research institute. Upon the successful conclusion of the program,  students are awarded a $1,000 stipend.

title: J. Craig Venter Institute Internship Program
text: The J. Craig Venter Institute (JCVI) Summer Internship Program provides an unparalleled opportunity for high school seniors to gain hands-on research experience under the guidance of renowned scientists. Participants engage in cutting-edge projects, collaborate with world-class researchers, and gain access to state-of-the-art facilities. This immersive experience fosters scientific curiosity, promotes critical thinking, and prepares students for success in STEM fields. The program's collaborative nature encourages teamwork and networking, building valuable relationships for future endeavors.

title: National Eye Institute Diversity in Vision Research and Ophthalmology Internship
text: The National Eye Institute's Diversity in Vision Research and Ophthalmology Internship (DIVRO) is a paid summer internship program that provides hands-on research experience to high school students from underrepresented groups in vision research. Interns will work closely with leading scientists at the NEI and participate in seminars and workshops to learn about the latest advances in vision research. This program is a great opportunity for students to gain valuable research experience and mentorship while exploring career options in vision research and ophthalmology.

title: NINDS Summer Internship Programs
text: The NINDS summer internship programs provide high school, undergraduate, graduate, and medical students with exceptional hands-on training and mentorship opportunities in neuroscience research. Interns collaborate directly with renowned scientists at the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke's Division of Intramural Research, gaining invaluable practical experience and exposure to cutting-edge research projects. These programs offer participants the chance to make significant contributions to scientific advancements and foster their passion for neuroscience.

title: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Summer Internship Program in Biomedical Research
text: The NHLBI Summer Internship Program in Biomedical Research is a 10-week opportunity for motivated high school students to conduct research alongside an expert at the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute. During the program, interns will develop critical science skills through mentorship, hands-on research experience, and engaging seminars covering advanced topics in biomedical research. This unparalleled experience provides students with a deep dive into the field of biomedical research, fostering their passion for science and preparing them for future endeavors in medicine, research, and other science-related professions.

title: Stanford Medicine Cardiothoracic Surgical Skills and Education Center Summer Internship
text: This internship is designed to educate high school students who are considering a career in medicine, science, and health by teaching them about cardiovascular anatomy and physiology and instructing them in medical and surgical techniques that will be utilized in their medical training.

title: USA Bio Olympiad
text: The USA Bio Olympiad (USABO) provides a high-caliber opportunity for high school students to excel in life sciences. Through rigorous online exams and an immersive training program, USABO cultivates students' passion for biology, equipping them with advanced concepts, lab skills, and the drive to succeed in international competitions. Participation in USABO not only fosters academic excellence but also opens doors to a wealth of opportunities in the field of biology.

title: International Brain Bee
text: The Brain Bee is an international neuroscience competition designed to captivate secondary school students who are fascinated by the complexities of the human brain. Participation in this esteemed competition not only fosters students' passion for brain science but also illuminates career pathways in the realm of biomedical research. Through a series of challenging and engaging questions, The Brain Bee ignites students' curiosity, encourages critical thinking, and inspires them to delve deeper into the captivating world of neuroscience. Ultimately, this prestigious competition empowers aspiring young minds to make significant contributions to the advancement of brain research and its profound implications for human health and well-being.

title: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program
text: The Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR) is an immersive, eight-week summer program designed to inspire high school students from diverse backgrounds to pursue careers in the sciences. Through hands-on research with esteemed Stanford faculty and researchers, students delve into cutting-edge biomedical projects, gaining invaluable experience in scientific inquiry and laboratory techniques. SIMR not only ignites a passion for medical research but also broadens perspectives, promotes inclusivity, and empowers students to make meaningful contributions to the field of medicine.

title: UCI x GATI
text: Participate in UCI x GATI, a prestigious program that nurtures the talents of exceptional high school students from diverse backgrounds. Based on the holistic assessment of students' abilities, GATI offers customized pathways to explore cutting-edge research in various fields like Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, and Biology. Through immersive summer and year-round programs, students engage with renowned UCI faculty, conduct research projects, and envision their future careers. As a GATI fellow, you'll join a vibrant community of like-minded peers and find a supportive network of mentors and educators who champion your academic growth. Seize this transformative opportunity to ignite your passion and shape your future as an innovative leader in your chosen field.

title: Regeneron ISEF
text: Regeneron ISEF, the world's largest international science and engineering fair, empowers high school students to explore their interests in STEM fields. Through local qualifying competitions, students showcase their original research projects alongside like-minded peers. Successful participants gain recognition for their hard work, often securing scholarships, awards, and opportunities for further research.

title: MIT Beaver Works Summer Institute (BWSI)
text: The MIT Beaver Works Summer Institute (BWSI) is a one-of-a-kind four-week summer program designed for high school students passionate about STEM. By providing project-based learning through engaging workshops, BWSI aids students in developing problem-solving and critical-thinking skills while fostering their interests in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. Participation in the program opens doors to unique research opportunities and collaborations with MIT faculty and researchers while immersing students in the vibrant learning environment of one of the world's leading academic institutions. By delving into hands-on projects, participants gain valuable experience and knowledge, solidifying their passion for STEM and preparing them for future endeavors in the field.

title: BioGENEius Challenges
text: The BioGENEius Challenges offer high school students a transformative opportunity to delve into cutting-edge scientific research and showcase their innovative ideas on an international stage. By participating in these challenges, students gain invaluable hands-on experience in biotechnology and connect with industry leaders in the field. The competition fosters creativity, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills, preparing students for success in STEM careers and empowering them to make a meaningful impact on the world.

title: Exploravision
text: ExploraVision engages young scientists in envisioning advancements in technology by fostering collaboration, critical thinking, and creativity. Participating students can connect with experts, gain valuable research and presentation skills, and earn recognition. The competition provides a platform for high schoolers to explore their passions, cultivate their scientific mindset, and prepare for future challenges in STEM fields.

title: Genes in Space
text: Calling aspiring scientists and problem solvers to join Genes in Space, an exciting competition where high school students design DNA analysis experiments to address real-world issues in space exploration. This unique contest provides an exceptional opportunity for students to develop their critical thinking, research skills, and creativity while contributing to the advancement of space science. The winning experiment will be conducted by astronauts on the International Space Station, offering participants the chance to witness their work making a tangible impact on space exploration. Don't miss this chance to be a part of this innovative and potentially life-changing experience.

title: Imagine Cup (Microsoft)
text: Imagine Cup is a global competition that empowers student developers to utilize their imaginations and technical abilities to address real-world issues. By providing a platform to showcase their innovative projects, the competition fosters creativity, collaboration, and problem-solving skills among high school students. Participation offers not only recognition and potential awards but also valuable experience in tackling global challenges through technology, fostering their growth as future STEM leaders.

title: Inventor’s Challenge
text: The Inventor's Challenge is an exciting competition that encourages high school students to use their creativity and problem-solving skills to develop innovative solutions. By participating, students can develop critical 21st-century skills such as creativity, innovation, optimism, and empathy. It also fosters a willingness to experiment and take risks, essential qualities for future leaders and innovators. The competition provides a platform for students to showcase their ideas, gain recognition for their work, and potentially win prizes that can support their educational and entrepreneurial endeavors.

title: International Genetically Engineered Machine
text: The International Genetically Engineered Machine (iGEM) competition is an international event designed for high school students interested in synthetic biology. Students work in teams to design, build, and test projects that advance the field. Through hands-on experience, students develop problem-solving, communication, and teamwork skills, while also learning about the latest in biotechnology. Participation in iGEM provides students with a unique opportunity to connect with world-renowned scientists, collaborate with students from diverse backgrounds, and gain international recognition for their achievements.

title: University of Chicago - Research in the Biological Sciences (RIBS)
text: The Research in the Biological Sciences (RIBS) program at the University of Chicago provides student the possibility to dive headfirst into research in molecular, microbiological, and cell biological techniques at one of the top universities in the United States. This practical experience, spanning four weeks, will give high school students a real-world glimpse into the methods used by working scientists and researchers. Not only will this program introduce participants to the field of biology, but it will further develop their skills in scientific research and critical thinking, giving the participants an edge in related fields they participate in.

title: Rose Hulman Institute of Technology - Operation Catapult
text: Immerse yourself in the world of science, technology, engineering, and math with Rose Hulman Institute of Technology's Operation Catapult program. This in-person summer program offers high school students the chance to explore fundamental scientific principles and engage with cutting-edge engineering systems while collaborating and socializing in a vibrant campus setting. It's an exceptional opportunity to enhance academic foundations, foster teamwork skills, and gain valuable insights into diverse STEM fields.

title: UC Davis Young Scholar Program (YSP)
text: Attend the acclaimed 5-week-long Young Summer Program at the prestigious University of California, Davis, and delve into original research in the captivating fields of natural sciences, environmental studies, and engineering. This transformative program welcomes 40 driven high school sophomores, offering the opportunity to earn 5 units of University Group Study Credit. Seize this exceptional chance to excel in the competitive college landscape.

title: Emory Summer Scholars Research Program
text: This six week Emory Summer Scholars Research Program internship is a deep dive into cancer-related research. Junior and senior students will have the opportunity to work side-by-side with mentors conducting groundbreaking research, gain hands-on lab experience, attend workshops, present their findings, and form lasting connections with cancer researchers.

title: Stanford STaRS Internship Program
text: The Stanford STaRS Internship Program offers talented high school juniors and seniors the opportunity to explore careers in healthcare and research. Participants work alongside experienced clinician/scientist mentors and peers, engaging in challenging and inspiring projects that provide hands-on experience in a supportive and collaborative environment. This program fosters intellectual growth, develops research skills, and provides valuable insights into the field of medicine.

title: Roswell Cancer Institute
text: If you're a high school junior, get first-hand scientific research experience to make those all-important decisions about a college science major and future career in science or healthcare.

title: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
text: High school students between ages 13–18 have an opportunity to submit a short video to share their original big scientific concepts in physics, biology, or math. This is a unique program that allows students to learn effective communication skills by working closely with a mentor throughout the competition. Not only can students potentially win scholarships and prizes, but they could also get published in a scientific journal.

title: Biomimicry Youth Design Challenge
text: Biomimicry Institute's Youth Design Challenge (YDC) empowers high school teams to design nature-inspired solutions to critical real-world problems. Through project-based learning, students learn biomimicry as an engineering design strategy, integrating STEM experiences aligned with Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS). YDC fosters creativity, critical thinking, and real-world problem-solving skills, preparing students for careers in science and engineering.

title: Hutton Junior Fisheries Biology Program
text: The Hutton Junior Fisheries Biology Program provides high school students from underrepresented groups an opportunity to explore careers in fisheries and aquatic science. Through an eight-week paid internship, students gain hands-on experience working alongside professional mentors in their local area. This program includes a $3,000 stipend, an all-expenses-paid trip to the Hutton Scholars Summit, and access to a network of mentors spanning across North America. Participating students develop valuable skills, learn about fisheries research and management, and gain a deeper understanding of the field.

title: YCCI Exposures Program
text: The Yale Center for Clinical Investigation (YCCI), in partnership with the Yale Cultural Ambassadors, offers a coveted summer research program, the YCCI Exposure Program. Harnessing the collective knowledge of a prestigious research hub and dedicated cultural ambassadors, this program presents a transformative opportunity for high school, undergraduate, and professional students. Participants immerse themselves in a dynamic STEM environment alongside internationally acclaimed scientists, unlocking an unparalleled learning experience in the realm of clinical and translational research. Through hands-on research involvement and mentorship from a multidisciplinary team, aspiring medical professionals gain invaluable insights, cultivate research skills, and cultivate their interest in healthcare disparities research.

title: Stanford Clinical Summer Internship
text: Attend Stanford Clinical Summer Internship to actively engage in exploring medicine and participate alongside dedicated and dynamic Stanford medical students, residents, and faculty. Immerse yourself in the art and science of world-class medical practice and gain practical experience that can help you advance your future career in healthcare professions. You'll make meaningful connections, learn from experienced professionals, and experience Stanford's unparalleled medical education environment.

title: Experiment and Explore: Summer Science Camp
text: This one-week summer camp is a great opportunity for the budding scientist! Students will work closely with two science faculty members as they explore biology, chemistry, and environmental science. They also get to hear from guest daily and work in labs to deepen their scientific understanding. This is a great way for students to get hands-on experience with science and learn about different career opportunities in the field.

title: U.S. National Chemistry Olympiad (USNCO)
text: The U.S. National Chemistry Olympiad (USNCO) is a prestigious competition for high school students with a passion for chemistry. participation in the USNCO offers numerous benefits, including the opportunity to showcase one's knowledge and skills, earn recognition for academic achievements, and gain valuable experience in preparing for college-level chemistry. The USNCO also helps students develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and teamwork abilities, which are essential for success in science and beyond.

title: NJCSTM Group Summer Scholars Research Program (GSSRP)
text: The NJCSTM Group Summer Scholars Research Program (GSSRP) offers an enriching hands-on research experience for talented high school students with a passion for STEM. The program's collaborative environment pairs participants with esteemed faculty and staff, exposing them to cutting-edge research practices in various disciplines, including Analytical Chemistry, Virtual Reality & Scientific Visualization, and Cancer Biology. By engaging in genuine experiments and working as part of a research team, students hone their technical skills, gain invaluable research knowledge, and discover their potential in scientific exploration.

title: MDI Biological Laboratory - High School Student Summer Research Fellowship
text: This fellowship offers a unique opportunity for high school students to gain hands-on research experience in a state-of-the-art laboratory. Students will work alongside experienced scientists, receive mentorship, and participate in cutting-edge research. This immersive program provides invaluable exposure to the scientific field, helps students develop essential research skills, and fosters their interest in pursuing careers in science.

title: Lillehei Heart Institute - Summer Research Scholars Program
text: The Lillehei Heart Institute offers annual summer research scholarships in basic science research related to cardiovascular disease. These highly competitive, prestigious scholarships are designed to expose highly qualified students to several disciplines within cardiovascular disease research and its clinical applications. Scholars will have the opportunity to work alongside world-renowned faculty, participate in cutting-edge research, and gain hands-on experience in a state-of-the-art research facility. This program is an excellent opportunity for students interested in pursuing a career in biomedical research.

title: University of California-Santa Cruz Science Internship Program
text: Aspiring STEM high school students seeking an immersive research experience should consider the UC-Santa Cruz Science Internship Program. Over the course of a 10-week summer program, students are paired with expert mentors and integrated into ongoing research projects at the university. Not only do participants gain valuable hands-on experience, they also have the opportunity to present their research at a symposium and network with professionals in their field. The program's alumni have gone on to attend prestigious universities and pursue successful careers in STEM fields.

title: Brower Youth Awards
text: Competing the work of six young leaders who are making studies in the environmental movement. As a signature element of Earth Island Institute’s year-round New Generation initiative, Brower Youth Award winners demonstrate excellent leadership as well as a commitment to the communities their work serves. By participating in this competition, high school students can gain recognition for their contributions to environmental protection and gain valuable skills in leadership and advocacy. The competition offers scholarships, mentorship opportunities, and the chance to connect with a network of like-minded individuals committed to making a difference in the world.

title: Climate Science Olympiad 2023
text: The Climate Science Olympiad is a fantastic opportunity for high school students passionate about climate change to showcase their knowledge, skills, and innovative ideas. Not only can participants win up to $15,000 in cash prizes, they also have the chance to present their solutions at the prestigious COP27 climate summit. The Olympiad empowers young people to become the climate leaders of tomorrow, equipping them with the experience and recognition they need to make a real difference in addressing the critical issue of climate change.

title: Eco Hero Awards
text: The Action for Nature non-profit annually rewards young people between the ages of 8 and 16 who have created innovative environmental projects. Participants have the chance to win cash prizes, certificates of achievement, and public recognition for their work. The competition is open to students worldwide and has been awarding top young environmentalists since 2003.

title: Fresh Films Video Challenge
text: Calling all high school students! Participate in Fresh Films Festival Video Challenge to explore documentary filmmaking, storytelling skills, and connect with others using your creative abilities. This challenge offers the opportunity to showcase your talents, gain valuable experience for college applications, and delve into environmental science topics. Unleash your creativity, express yourself, and discover the transformative power of storytelling through film.

title: Genius Olympiad
text: The GENIUS Olympiad offers high school students a unique opportunity to showcase their environmental projects on a global stage. Through this competition, students can develop their research and communication skills, gain recognition for their work, and connect with peers who share their passion for environmental stewardship. Participation in the GENIUS Olympiad can foster innovation, promote environmental awareness, and inspire students to pursue careers in STEM fields related to the environment.

title: Penn Climate Venture
text: Calling all budding climate innovators! The PCV Prize offers high school students a unique opportunity to showcase their climate tech startup ideas and make a positive environmental impact. Join the competition for expert mentorship, valuable connections with venture capitalists, and a chance to win prize money that can kickstart your entrepreneurial journey. Whether you're passionate about renewable energy, sustainable transportation, or environmental conservation, the PCV Prize provides a platform to develop your ideas and contribute to a greener future.

title: Planet 911 Youth Film Challenge
text: The Planet 911 Youth Film Challenge is a competition for filmmakers aged 10-22 that encourages them to create films that raise awareness about environmental issues and propose solutions. By participating, students can hone their filmmaking skills, showcase their environmental concerns, and potentially win cash prizes for themselves and their schools or organizations. The competition provides a platform for young voices to be heard and empowers them to advocate for positive change in the fight against climate change and environmental degradation.

title: Science Without Borders Challenge - International Art Contest
text: The Science Without Borders® Challenge invites high school students, ages 11-19, to harness their creativity and engage in ocean conservation through art. This international competition fosters environmental awareness and inspires students to contribute to the preservation of aquatic resources. By participating, students gain recognition for their artistic talents, potentially earning scholarships up to $500 for their outstanding entries while fostering a passion for ocean conservation.

title: Youth Making Ripples Video Contest
text: High school students are encouraged to participate in the Youth Making Ripples Film Competition to showcase their creativity and passion for marine conservation. This opportunity allows students to develop their filmmaking skills, foster their understanding of marine science, and contribute to the broader conversation around ocean preservation. By submitting a film under five minutes in length, students can explore diverse marine topics, address critical issues, or inspire action for a healthier future for our oceans and planet.

title: ECI Americas Fellowship
text: The ECI Americas Fellowship is a free virtual course for youth ages 12-18 based in North, South, or Central America, The hands on, action-based learning program focuses on the principles of intersectional environmentalism and leadership. Fellows will learn about pressing environmental issues, develop their leadership skills, and use this combined knowledge to create their own independent initatives. This is a great opportunity for teenage students to get involved in enviornmentalism and leadership, as the course will teach them valuable skills and allow them to stay engaged in their communities for future environmentally focused projects.

title: Carnegie Museums Internships
text: Participation in the Carnegie Museums Internships offers high school students a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in the museum field. Interns will work in public-facing or behind-the-scenes positions, developing valuable skills in communication, collaboration, and problem-solving. Through interactions with museum staff and visitors, interns will expand their professional network and gain insights into various museum departments. This enriching experience will prepare them for future careers in arts, culture, or related fields.

title: World Series of Innovation (WSI)
text: Calling all creative, solution-oriented high school students! Join the World Series of Innovation (WSI) and make a real impact. As part of the UN Global Compact, WSI offers an extraordinary platform to showcase your brilliance. Work with professionals, develop groundbreaking solutions for pressing global issues, and benefit from exclusive mentorship opportunities. Rise to the challenge and emerge as a leader in innovation while shaping a better future for generations to come.

title: River of Words Contest
text: The River of Words Contest is an international, free poetry and art competition for students ages 5-19 that encourages them to express their thoughts about the environment through their work. High school students, particularly, will find participation highly rewarding as it gives them a platform to showcase their creativity, earn recognition for their artistic abilities, and compete for prestigious awards, including scholarships and the chance for their work to be published in a renowned anthology.

title: National Wildlife Habitat Education Program
text: High schoolers can join the National Wildlife Habitat Education Program (WHEP), a friendly competition where teams of three to four individuals test their wildlife knowledge. The winning senior team from each participating state qualifies for the national contest typically held during the last full week of July. Not only does WHEP provide a stimulating learning experience, but it also offers an exclusive opportunity for high school seniors to engage in a national level competition, broadening their perspectives on environmental science and fostering a deeper understanding of wildlife conservation.

title: NCF Envirothon
text: The NCF Envirothon is an environmental and natural resource competition designed to give high school students hands-on experience in solving environmental challenges. The competition tasks teams with completing various natural resource challenges, including written tests, field studies, and oral presentations. NCF Envirothon participants create inventive solutions to environmental and natural resource issues facing our world today. In addition to enhancing conservation skills and knowledge, students are empowered to educate others, act in their communities, choose environmental disciplines for high education, and aim toward careers in the environment, natural resources, and conservation.

title: CDC Museum Disease Detective Camp
text: CDC Museum Disease Detective Camp (DDC) is an interdisciplinary educational program that allows students to become immersed in the field of public health. Open to high school juniors and seniors, the camp provides an opportunity for students to learn about the work of the CDC and gain hands-on experience in disease detection. Through interactive activities and discussions with experts, students will explore topics such as epidemiology, microbiology, and global health. Participation in the camp not only provides valuable educational experiences but also fosters critical thinking, problem-solving, and leadership skills. The DDC program is a competitive and rewarding opportunity for students interested in pursuing careers in public health or related fields.

title: National Geographic Student Travel
text: National Geographic Student Travel is an incredible opportunity for high school students to embark on an educational adventure that will inspire them to become the next generation of explorers. Through this program, students join National Geographic experts in the field, gaining hands-on experience in environmental science, photography, and filmmaking. As part of the On Assignment project, students engage in meaningful work, making real contributions to scientific research and conservation efforts. By participating in this transformative experience, students develop a deep understanding of the world and their place in it, fostering a lifelong passion for exploration and conservation.

title: AgDiscovery Program
text: High school students interested in exploring agriculture may benefit from the AgDiscovery program. This free summer opportunity allows teenagers to reside on college grounds for two to four weeks. They will engage with professors, USDA professionals, and participate in interactive experiences such as laboratories, workshops, and excursions. In addition to gaining hands-on exposure to agricultural practices, participants will participate in team-building and character-building exercises. The program provides exceptional chances for students to explore their career possibilities within an agricultural context by introducing them to varied and dynamic experts within the industry. Students will have the opportunity to interact with plant and animal scientists, veterinarians, wildlife biologists, and administrative staff members to better understand the diverse range of opportunities available within agriculture. AgDiscovery offers an insightful and immersive experience for those considering a future in agriculture. Don't miss out on this thrilling chance to explore the possibilities in this expanding domain.

title: Young Filmmakers Contest
text: High school students can participate in the One Earth Film Festival's Young Filmmakers Contest, which recognizes films that promote sustainable solutions to environmental problems.  By participating, students have the opportunity to showcase their understanding of environmental issues and their solutions. Through the contest, students can enhance their research and communication skills and gain recognition for their work.

title: American Mathematics Competitions (AMC)
text: The American Mathematics Competitions (AMC) 10 and AMC 12 are 25-question, 75-minute, multiple-choice examinations designed to promote the development and enhancement of problem-solving skills in high school mathematics. The competitions provide an exciting opportunity for students to challenge themselves, measure their skills against their peers, and qualify for a series of subsequent competitions, including the USAMO, USJMO, and IMO. Participation in the AMC is an excellent way for students to improve their critical thinking, problem-solving, and analytical skills, which can benefit them in various academic and professional pursuits.

title: M3 Math Modeling Challenge
text: MathWorks Math Modeling Challenge (M3 Challenge) is a free, online competition for high school juniors and seniors in the U.S. and sixth form students in England and Wales. Participants in this challenge apply mathematical modeling to a real-world problem, an excellent way to explore potential career paths in the field. No fees are associated with participation in this challenge. Successful participation is a great addition to college and even scholarship applications.

title: PROMYS | Program in Mathematics for Young Scientists
text: PROMYS is a six-week summer program in mathematics for powerfully self-motivated high school students. Founded in 1989, PROMYS is a residential program held on the campus of Boston University with roughly 80 high school students and 25 undergraduate counselors. PROMYS fosters the development of mathematical talent and builds a community of budding mathematicians. Students who participate in PROMYS will have the opportunity to develop their problem-solving skills, critical thinking abilities, and mathematical knowledge at an advanced level, setting them apart as highly desirable future college and graduate school applicants.

title: The Ross Mathematics Program
text: The Ross Mathematics Program is a highly selective summer program designed for high-achieving high school students with a strong passion for mathematics. Through a rigorous curriculum centered around daily problem sets in number theory, the program cultivates critical thinking, problem-solving abilities, and mathematical maturity. By engaging with open-ended questions and investigating them in depth, participants develop a profound understanding of mathematical concepts and an ability to apply them to novel situations. The program provides an exceptional platform for students to deepen their mathematical knowledge, enhance their analytical skills, and foster a lasting love for the subject.
