title: Mathcamp
text: Canada/USA Mathcamp is an immersive summer program designed to challenge and inspire mathematically talented high school students from around the world. This exceptional program provides an environment that fosters intellectual growth, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Through engaging lectures, hands-on workshops, and collaborative projects, students immerse themselves in advanced mathematical concepts, develop a deeper understanding of mathematics, and connect with fellow enthusiasts who share their passion for the subject. Participation in this prestigious program not only enriches students' mathematical knowledge but also broadens their horizons, promotes teamwork, and cultivates a lifelong appreciation for the power of mathematics.

title: AwesomeMath
text: The AwesomeMath summer camp offers a unique opportunity for mathematically gifted high school students to immerse themselves in an intellectually stimulating and rigorous learning environment. Designed to challenge and inspire, the camp features advanced topics not typically covered in school, broadening students' mathematical knowledge and fostering their problem-solving abilities. Participants will engage in interactive lectures, collaborate with peers from around the world, and develop their mathematical thinking skills under the guidance of experienced educators. By participating in AwesomeMath, high school students will gain a deeper understanding of mathematics, enhance their problem-solving skills, and connect with a global community of like-minded individuals.

title: The Hampshire College Summer Studies in Mathematics
text: HCSSiM is an intensive six-week residential program for talented high school students passionate about mathematics. Participants engage in challenging mathematical concepts and exploration, fostering critical thinking, problem-solving, and a deep understanding of the subject. They benefit from expert instruction, mentorship, and a collaborative learning environment, preparing them for advanced mathematics studies and future careers in STEM fields.

title: ASA Statistics Project Competition
text: The American Statistical Association (ASA) hosts an annual Project Competition for high school students, encouraging them to explore statistics and probability through real-world projects. By participating, students gain valuable skills in data analysis, communication, and problem-solving. The competition provides a platform for showcasing their research, fostering critical thinking, and inspiring future careers in STEM fields.

title: Caribou Mathematics Competition
text:
The Caribou Mathematics Competition is a world wide online contest that is held six times throughout the school year. Each of these days, five contests are offered, one for each of the grade levels 3/4, 5/6, 7/8, 9/10 and 11/12 and each one in English, French and Persian.

The Caribou Cup is the series of all Caribou Contests in one school year. Each student's ranking in the Caribou Cup is determined by their performance in their best 5 of 6 contests through the school year.

title: Carnegie Mellon Informatics and Mathematics Competition
text: The Carnegie Mellon Informatics and Mathematics Competition (CMIMC) is an annual contest held at Carnegie Mellon University. CMIMC serves as a platform for high school students to demonstrate their mathematical and computational problem-solving skills. Participants engage in various events designed to challenge and expand their knowledge. The competition offers a rewarding experience for aspiring mathematicians and computer scientists, fostering their passion for STEM fields and providing valuable exposure to university-level challenges.

title: Comap Mathematical Contest in Modeling
text: The COMAP Mathematical Contest in Modeling (MCM) and Interdisciplinary Contest in Modeling (ICM) are international competitions that challenge high school students and college undergraduates to apply their problem-solving, critical thinking, and research skills to solve real-world problems. By participating in these contests, students can enhance their analytical, modeling, and communication abilities, while also gaining experience in teamwork and time management. Additionally, successful participants can receive recognition for their accomplishments and may be eligible for scholarships and awards.

title: Cooper Hewitt National High School Design Competition
text: Calling all high school design students! Unleash your creativity and innovation in the Cooper Hewitt National High School Design Competition. Embrace the challenge of using design and data to make a positive impact in your community. Showcase your skills by creating a compelling design sketch and description that demonstrates how your solution addresses a pressing local issue. The competition offers a platform to showcase your talent, foster critical thinking, and contribute to your community's well-being. Don't miss this opportunity to harness the power of design for good!

title: Harvard MIT Mathematics Tournament
text: The Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament (HMMT) is among the world's most prestigious and well-attended high school mathematics competitions, annually drawing about 1,000 students internationally. It provides an exceptional platform for motivated high school students to challenge their mathematical abilities and engage with peers who share their passion for the subject. This prestigious tournament is entirely student-organized by students from Harvard, MIT, and neighboring schools. Many of these organizers are former HMMT participants, demonstrating the competition's enduring impact and the strong community it fosters.

title: Johns Hopkins Mathematics Tournament
text: The Johns Hopkins Math Tournament (JHMT) is an annual math competition open to area high school students. Contestants take two 45-minute proof rounds and two hour-long individual tests. This is a great opportunity for high school students to challenge themselves mathematically and earn recognition for their achievements. Top-performing students can qualify for invitations to prestigious summer programs and scholarships. The tournament also provides a venue for students to connect with like-minded peers and explore their passion for mathematics in a fun and competitive environment.

title: Wharton Data Science Academy
text: The Wharton Data Science Academy is a competitive summer program for high school juniors and sophomores. The program teaches students essential data science techniques, such as data wrangling and data mining, using the R programming language. Students will have a chance to use advanced techniques such as natural language processing and machine learning. Through this program, students will apply their learned techniques to solve real-world problems. The academy will develop students' data science skills, critical thinking abilities, and communication skills.

title: Texas State University Honors Summer Math Camp
text: The Mathworks Honors Summer Math Camp is a remarkable immersive learning opportunity, preparing high school students for success in STEM-related fields. This intensive multi-summer program fosters the development of talented students from all socioeconomic backgrounds. By providing in-depth mathematical experiences, HSMC equips participants with essential skills for future degrees and careers in mathematics, science, engineering, and beyond.

title: Princeton Program in Algorithmic and Combinatorial Thinking
text: The Princeton Program in Algorithmic and Combinatorial Thinking is an in-person summer program suitable for all grade levels. Focusing primarily on theoretical topics, the program imbues students with a rigorous foundation in mathematics through engaging courses in discrete mathematics, proof techniques, and graph theory. Through thought-provoking problem-solving exercises and guidance from expert instructors, students sharpen their critical thinking skills, strengthen their understanding of mathematical concepts, and gain a competitive edge in STEM fields.

title: F=ma (USAPHO)
text: F=ma is an annual physics competition organized by the American Association of Physics Teachers. High school students who participate in this competition have the opportunity to engage in challenging and enriching physics problems, develop their critical thinking and problem-solving skills, and gain a deeper understanding of physics concepts. The competition also provides students with the opportunity to connect with other physics enthusiasts and potentially earn recognition for their achievements.

title: The American Rocketry Challenge
text: The American Rocketry Challenge (ARC) is an annual competition that encourages high school students to explore the fields of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). Through hands-on experience designing, building, and launching rockets, students gain invaluable knowledge in aerospace engineering, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, and physics. The ARC provides an engaging and competitive platform for students to showcase their skills, collaborate with peers, and discover their passion for STEM. Participation in the ARC fosters critical thinking, problem-solving, and teamwork, preparing students for future success in STEM-related careers.

title: Ocean Bowl
text:
The National Oceanic and Asmhopheres Administration's (NOAA) National Byline for Science and Engineering Fair competition, or the "OceanBowl," is a highly-regarded competition that gives high school students a chance to:

- Immerse themselves in ocean science.
- Use critical thinking, problem-solving, and team work skills.
- Build a foundation in environmental and earth science areas.
- Prepare for college and careers in ocean science, engineering, and other scientific and environmental fields.
- Become leaders in activities that safeguard the waters near the coasts.

title: AAPT High School Physics Photo Contest
text: The AAPT High School Physics Photo Contest is a prestigious international competition that challenges students to capture the beauty of physics through photography. By participating in this contest, students can develop their creativity, problem-solving abilities, and scientific inquiry skills. Winners receive recognition, prizes, and the opportunity to showcase their work to a global audience.

title: Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory Internship
text: The Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory Internship offers high school seniors the unique opportunity to engage in research alongside experts in physics and engineering. Interns work on projects under the guidance of the lab's research staff, gaining hands-on experience in a state-of-the-art laboratory. The internship fosters scientific inquiry, develops problem-solving skills, and provides insights into potential career paths in STEM fields.

title: Adopt-a-Physicist
text: The Adopt-a-Physicist program connects high school physics students with real physics graduates who are eager to share their stories. The participating physicists embody a range of careers, backgrounds, interests, and educational levels, providing a unique opportunity for students to learn about the diverse possibilities within the field of physics. Through online discussion forums, students engage in lively and in-depth conversations with physicists, gaining insights into their career paths and perspectives on the world of science.

title: International Young Physicists’ Tournament
text: The International Young Physicists’ Tournament (IYPT) is an international competition for high school students interested in physics. Participants work in teams to solve open-ended physics problems, then present their findings and defend them before a panel of judges. IYPT is a unique opportunity for students to develop their problem-solving skills, critical thinking abilities, and communication skills. Participation in IYPT can also help students to develop their interest in physics and to pursue careers in science and engineering.

title: Aerospace Robotics Competition
text: Through the Aerorobotics Competition, high school students gain invaluable hands-on experience in the exciting field of aerospace engineering. By collaborating with university students and industry professionals, participants develop essential skills such as technical writing, flight control, autonomous programming, and project management. This multi-tiered competition fosters leadership, innovation, and a deep understanding of the principles and applications of aerospace engineering, preparing students for future success in STEM education or careers.

title: Reach for the Stars - National Rocket Competition
text: The Reach for the Stars National Rocket Competition, sponsored by AIAA, offers a unique opportunity for high school students to engage in aerospace engineering and hands-on experimentation. Participants build and launch rockets, aiming for precision landings near target zones. The competition fosters teamwork, problem-solving, and an understanding of STEM concepts. By participating, students can showcase their abilities, prepare for potential careers in aerospace, and inspire future generations to reach for the stars.

title: Real World Design Challenge
text: Calling all high schoolers with a passion for engineering! The Real World Design Challenge (RWDC) offers an exceptional opportunity to tackle pressing industry challenges while honing your skills in a collaborative setting. Through this competition, students can apply their knowledge, develop innovative solutions using professional software, and showcase their creativity through impactful presentations. Participation in RWDC not only fosters critical thinking and problem-solving abilities but also provides a glimpse into the exciting world of engineering and potential career paths in the field.

title: Student Unmanned Aerial Systems Competition
text: High school students gain invaluable experience in aerospace engineering, computer science, electrical engineering, and robotics through this competition. Students learn to design, integrate, and demonstrate an unmanned aerial system (UAS) capable of autonomous flight and navigation. Developed skills include remote sensing with onboard payload sensors and executing specific tasks. The competition provides a platform for students to showcase their innovation and problem-solving abilities. Participation enhances technical skills, promotes teamwork, and fosters problem-solving. Since 2002, the Student Unmanned Aerial Systems Competition has provided a unique opportunity for students to develop their talents.

title: Zero Robotics
text: Zero Robotics is an exceptional robotics competition that offers high school students the unparalleled opportunity to program real robots aboard the International Space Station. Through this immersive experience, students not only develop their technical skills in aerospace engineering, computer science, and robotics but also gain hands-on knowledge of real-world space exploration. The competition fosters critical thinking, problem-solving abilities, and collaboration skills, preparing students for future careers in STEM fields.

title: 120 Hours Architecture Competition
text: 120 HOURS is an independent architecture competition for high school students organized on a non-profit, voluntary basis without the involvement of a school administration. The competition provides high school students with a unique opportunity to showcase their talents, gain valuable experience in architectural competitions, and connect with top universities and industry professionals. The competition is challenging and fun to participate in, and offers a relevant first encounter with architectural competitions.

title: AFSF Design Ideas Collective
text: The AFSF Design Ideas Collective empowers high school students to harness the power of design thinking to tackle real-world challenges. This unique competition invites students to develop innovative and sustainable solutions to pressing societal issues. Participants gain valuable skills in critical thinking, problem-solving, and collaboration while contributing to a brighter future for all.

title: Architecture at Zero
text: The Architecture at Zero competition for 2023 challenges high school students to help shape the future of decarbonization, resilience, and equity in architecture. Students will work on designing a building that will serve as a regenerative agricultural learning hub which will help teach and implement climate adaptive and sustainable agriculture. The graduate and professionals level division includes designing residential housing for farm students and staff on site. Students can enter for no cost and can win awards up to $10,000.

title: International Bridge Building Contest
text: The International Bridge Building Contest provides participating high school students with a unique and engaging opportunity to refine their problem-solving abilities, strengthen their critical thinking skills, and learn the principles of physics in an interactive and memorable way. The competition fosters hands-on experience in bridge construction and places an emphasis on developing engineering design skills. It serves as an excellent extracurricular pursuit that supports in-class learning and offers valuable insights into the field of engineering, while also promoting academic collaboration at a statewide level.

title: SchoolsNEXT Design Competition
text: High school students are invited to participate in the SchoolsNEXT Design Competition, an international annual opportunity to showcase their creativity in planning and designing learning environments. The competition emphasizes the importance of sustainable and resilient schools that foster student and teacher achievement and enhance community vitality. Student teams are challenged to design their learning environments, considering factors such as resource conservation, environmental responsiveness, and community engagement. By participating, students develop their skills in multi-disciplinary planning and design, presenting their projects to a jury of professionals for review, and potentially winning recognition for their innovative ideas.

title: UIUC Discover FAA High School Competitions
text: Students in grades 9-12 who elect to participate in the FAA high school competitions have the potential opportunity to compete to win a scholarship to the college's degree programs or their summer program. Students interested in the arts, architecture, music, or performing can submit works across categories including a self portrait, architural drawing, or an elaborate choreography for review. Participating is a great way to boost a college application and stand out to potential employers.

title: Summer@Rensselaer Architecture Career Discovery Program
text: This exciting two-week online program offers high school students an unparalleled opportunity to experience the dynamic world of architecture at one of the nation's top-ranked architecture schools. Through interactive classes, students will gain hands-on knowledge in architecture theory, computer modeling, sketching, and design principles. They will engage with experienced architecture faculty and benefit from interactions with peers from various backgrounds. Participation in this program can significantly enhance a student's understanding of architecture as a career path and provide a competitive edge for their future academic and professional endeavors.

title: The American Computer Science League
text: American Computer Science League (ACSL) organizes computer programming and computer science contests for K-12 schools, organizations and local groups. The 2022-2023 school year will be our 45th year of continuous operation! Last year, over 700 teams in the United States, Canada, Europe, and Asia participated.

title: CyberPatriot
text: CyberPatriort is a National Youth Cyber Education Program geared towards inspiring K-12 students to pursue careers in cybersecurity and other STEM-related disciplines. Its core program is the National Youth Cyber Defense Competition, the nation's largest cyber defense competition, where teams of high school and middle school students implement cybersecurity controls on a virtual environment, fend off simulated cyber-attacks, and build incident response and recovery plans. Participation in CyberPatriort provides students with hands-on experience in cybersecurity, develops their problem-solving and critical thinking skills, and prepares them for future careers in the field. If you're a high school student interested in cybersecurity, consider joining CyberPatriort to explore your passion, gain valuable skills, and connect with professionals in the industry.

title: First Robotics Competition
text: FIRST Robotics Competition combines the excitement of sports with the challenges of science and technology. Teams of high school students design, build, and program industrial-size robots to play a challenging field game against other teams. This hands-on experience provides students with valuable skills in teamwork, problem-solving, and engineering. Under strict rules, limited time, and resources, students learn to raise funds, design a team "brand," and hone their teamwork skills. The competition encourages students to pursue careers in science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM). It also provides a platform for students to develop their leadership, communication, and critical thinking skills. Additionally, the competition offers scholarship opportunities and can help students earn college credit.

title: VEX Robotics
text: The VEX Robotics competition is an engaging and enriching experience that ignites a passion for STEM within high school students. Through hands-on construction and competitive play, participants develop invaluable skills in problem-solving, critical thinking, teamwork, and innovation. The competition fosters a love for science, technology, engineering, and math, equipping students with the knowledge and confidence to excel in future STEM careers. With tournaments held throughout the year, the program culminates in the prestigious VEX Robotics World Championship, providing an unparalleled platform for showcasing exceptional robotics creations.

title: USA Computing Olympiad (USACO)
text: The USA Computing Olympiad (USACO) provides high school students with an extraordinary opportunity to develop and showcase their computing skills. Through USACO, students gain access to top-notch training resources and six online competitions throughout the year. Additionally, USACO offers summer training camps for top students to enhance their abilities and prepare for the International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI), the most renowned algorithmic programming competition for high school students globally. Participating in USACO allows students to challenge themselves, build their programming proficiency, and potentially represent their country on the international stage.

title: Project: Empower
text: Project: Empower is a non-profit organization that connects students to underprivileged communities through software creation. It's a fantastic opportunity for high school students to make a real difference in the world by applying their computer science skills and fostering a passion for community service.

title: Girls Who Code
text: Girls Who Code is an exceptional program designed for high school students, providing them with immersive experiences and empowering them in the field of computer science. Through the program's transformative platform, young women and non-binary individuals gain valuable skills and knowledge, fostering creativity and innovation within the technological landscape. By fostering a supportive and inclusive environment, Girls Who Code allows students to make meaningful connections while exploring their interests in a structured and engaging manner. This comprehensive program offers a gateway for high school students to enhance their technological literacy, preparing them for future success in STEM fields and shaping the next generation of leaders in the digital realm.

title: MIT Women's Technology Program
text: Participating in the MIT Women's Technology Program offers numerous benefits for high school students. It provides an immersive and hands-on exploration of engineering through classes, labs, and projects. Students gain valuable experience and skills in computer science, electrical engineering, and mechanical engineering, while also fostering their creativity and teamwork abilities. The program creates a supportive and empowering environment for young women to engage with MIT faculty and students, inspiring them to pursue careers in STEM fields and develop their leadership potential.

title: UNH-IOL High School Summer Internship Program
text: UNH's HighTech Bound Summer Internship Program offers rising high school seniors an immersive experience in network technologies. This paid 4-6 week opportunity allows ambitious students to participate in cutting-edge research projects and gain invaluable work experience alongside industry professionals. Through this program, students can cultivate their technical skills, nurture their passion for STEM, and explore potential career paths in the technology sector.

title: AI4ALL
text: High school students looking to make an impact through AI can apply to AI4ALL Summer Programs. Immerse in hands-on learning, gain mentorship from top AI practitioners, and build a supportive peer network at top universities. This opportunity empowers students to develop their skills, solve problems they care about, and shape the future of AI.

title: Aerial Drone Competition
text: The Aerial Drone Competition is an engaging and educational event designed to nurture hands-on, student-centric learning. High school teams delving into this competition gain valuable insights into drones, flight dynamics, programming, documentation, and communication. Participation in this competition ignites passions for STEM fields, cultivates technical skills, and provides exposure to potential drone-related career opportunities, empowering students to explore the thrilling world of aerial technology.

title: APL Problem Solving Competition
text: The APL Problem-Solving Competition, hosted by Dyalog Ltd., offers an exciting opportunity for high school students to sharpen their programming skills and engage in problem-solving challenges. With a total prize pool of USD 6,500 and the chance to attend an exclusive user meeting, this competition provides a platform for students to showcase their talents and win recognition for their achievements.

title: Bell Advanced Vertical Robotics Competition
text: The Bell Advanced Vertical Robotics Competition offers high school students a unique opportunity to develop valuable skills in STEM fields. By designing, building, and competing with cutting-edge aerial robotics technology, students gain hands-on experience in computer science, electrical engineering, and mechanical engineering. This immersive program prepares participants for future careers in the rapidly growing STEM workforce, equipping them with the skills and knowledge needed to excel in the fields of ground and aerial robotics.

title: Best Robotics Challenge
text: The Best Robotics Competition presents a compelling opportunity for high school students to hone their critical STEM skills. Each year, participating teams design and build robots to navigate a unique challenge field with varying obstacles and tasks. The tournament-style format fosters teamwork, problem-solving, and innovation. Competing in this annual event not only enhances technical abilities but also cultivates leadership, cooperation, and perseverance -- invaluable qualities for future success in STEM fields and beyond.

title: Botball
text: Botball is an educational robotics competition that engages high school students in a team-oriented environment. Through hands-on, inquiry-based learning, Botball develops students' leadership, teamwork, and problem-solving skills. By integrating with common core standards, Botball provides a unique platform for students to apply their knowledge in science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) while fostering their creativity, discipline, and passion for robotics.

title: MATE ROV Competition
text: The MATE ROV Competition offers an exceptional opportunity for high school students to engage in a hands-on STEM challenge. By designing and building Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs), students develop critical thinking, problem-solving, teamwork, and technical skills. This competition provides a platform for students to apply their knowledge in real-world scenarios, inspiring them to pursue careers in science, engineering, and technology.

title: North American Computational Linguistics Olympiad
text: The North American Computational Linguistics Olympiad (NACLO) presents high school students with an unparalleled opportunity to delve into the fascinating world of computational linguistics and natural language processing. By engaging in this competition, students not only sharpen their logic skills but also gain invaluable insights into the complexities and diversity of human language. NACLO's meticulously crafted problems, designed by experts in the field, expose students to cutting-edge research and foster their interest in pursuing higher education and careers in STEM disciplines related to language.

title: RoboBoat
text: The RoboBoat Competition challenges student teams to design and build Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASV) for an international competition. Through hands-on engineering and robotics experience, students develop technical skills, learn teamwork and problem-solving, and discover the cutting-edge field of autonomous maritime technology. Participation provides a unique opportunity for high schoolers to explore STEM fields, foster innovation, and compete with peers on a global stage, potentially leading to scholarships, future educational opportunities, and industry recognition.

title: Sea, Air, and Land Challenge
text: The Sea, Air, and Land Challenge, sponsored by the Office of Naval Research, provides an exceptional opportunity for high school students to delve into the engineering process and showcase their design capabilities. By engaging in this competition, students embark on a comprehensive journey, designing systems relevant to the Department of Defense, honing their problem-solving skills, and developing a deep understanding of engineering concepts. The challenges presented are modeled after real-world missions faced by military, national security agencies, and first responders, ensuring that students gain practical experience and context for their learning.

title: Solar Car Challenge
text: The Solar Car Challenge is a competition that motivates high school students to pursue careers in science and engineering while promoting awareness of alternative energy sources.  Teams of students design and build solar-powered cars which are then raced against each other. The experience allows students to apply their knowledge in a practical setting, develop problem-solving skills, and work as part of a team.

title: National Robotics Challenge
text: The National Robotics Challenge is a renowned competition for students in grades 6 through graduate school. High school participants can showcase their engineering skills by designing, building, and programming robots for various challenges. The contest fosters creativity, problem-solving abilities, and collaboration. Winners receive recognition, prizes, and opportunities to advance in the robotics field. Participating in the National Robotics Challenge provides a platform for students to interact with peers and mentors, develop valuable skills, and potentially secure future scholarships or career opportunities.

title: Virginia Tech High School Programming Contest
text: Virginia Tech University offers a free Computer Science programming contest for high school students in Virginia and beyond. The contest is modeled after the ICPC and gives students the opportunity to showcase their programming skills. The competition is open to teams of students who are coached by a teacher or parent. The contest registration deadline is in November, and awards are given to top-performing teams. By participating in this engaging contest, students will not only enhance their programming skills but also interact with computer science professionals and explore future opportunities in the field.

title: World Robot Olympiad
text: The World Robot Olympiad (WRO) offers high school students an extraordinary opportunity to hone their problem-solving abilities, cultivate their creativity, and forge unforgettable memories. Through engaging robotics competitions, WRO empowers students to engineer innovative solutions, foster teamwork and collaboration, and develop their aptitude in STEM disciplines. Participation in WRO competitions equips students with invaluable skills that empower them both within and beyond the classroom.
