title: CodeQuest
text: CodeQuest is a fantastic opportunity for high school students to engage in a challenging and rewarding computer programming experience. This annual competition hosted by Lockheed Martin fosters teamwork, problem-solving skills, and proficiency in multiple programming languages. Participation in CodeQuest not only allows students to demonstrate their technical abilities but also provides valuable insights into the field of computer programming and its potential career paths within the industry.

title: RoboCup
text: RoboCup is an international competition challenging teams of students to design, build, and program autonomous robots to play soccer, promoting robotics and AI research. For high school students, RoboCup offers an invaluable opportunity to develop their creativity, problem-solving skills, and teamwork abilities. By participating, students gain invaluable practical experience in robotics, engineering, and computer science, fostering their interest in STEM fields. Additionally, they have the chance to connect with peers and mentors, expanding their knowledge and network.

title: Cyber Defense Training Camp
text: Cyber Defense Training Camp is an in-person, 7-day residential program designed for high school students interested in cybersecurity. Participants will gain practical skills and expand their knowledge through instruction by an experienced security professional. They will learn about career options in the field, take field trips, and hear from speakers to prepare for a potential career in cybersecurity.

title: National Cyber League
text: The National Cyber League (NCL) provides high school students with exceptional opportunities to refine their cybersecurity acumen while also gaining a competitive edge in the industry. Through challenging and engaging competitions, students showcase their proficiency in mitigating security threats, investigating digital evidence, and resolving cybersecurity emergencies. Participation not only enhances their technical skills but also enables them to identify areas for improvement and career development. By honing their abilities through the NCL, high school students position themselves for academic and professional success in the growing field of cybersecurity.

title: Lincoln Laboratory Cipher Program
text: The Lincoln Laboratory Cipher Program is a free one-week summer workshop for high school students interested in mathematics or cybersecurity. Students will learn how to build secure encryption schemes and digital signatures. They will also learn about recent developments in cryptography, such as homomorphic encryption and multi-party computation. This program is a great opportunity for students to learn about a fascinating and rapidly developing field.

title: US Cyber Challenge: Cyber Quests
text: US Cyber Challenge: Cyber Quests presents an extraordinary opportunity for high school students to hone their cybersecurity prowess through a series of captivating online competitions. These quests delve into the complexities of vulnerability analysis, forensic and packet capture analysis, challenging participants to demonstrate their knowledge and skills in various aspects of information security. Designed to accommodate diverse skill levels, these quests cater to both beginners and advanced students, providing a valuable platform for students to showcase their talents, explore their interests, and prepare for careers in the ever-evolving field of cybersecurity.

title: University of Pennsylvania – Jerome Fisher Management and Technology Summer Institute (M&T)
text: University of Pennsylvania's Management & Technology Summer Institute provides an opportunity for rising high school seniors and juniors to explore the intersection of business and technology. The program combines academic rigor with hands-on experience, allowing students to develop their critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills while gaining valuable insights into the latest industry trends. By participating in the M&TSI, students can gain a competitive edge for their future academic and professional pursuits.

title: Kidwind Challenge
text: The KidWind Challenge is a thrilling and educational competition for high school students globally. By partaking in this challenge, students delve into the world of renewable energy, specifically wind and solar power. They have the opportunity to work in teams, designing, building, and testing their own miniature wind turbines and solar structures. This challenge sparks their curiosity, cultivates critical thinking skills, and fosters teamwork. Furthermore, it inspires students to explore sustainable energy solutions and promotes environmental awareness. With global recognition and support available, the KidWind Challenge provides a valuable platform for students to showcase their creativity, ingenuity, and problem-solving abilities, preparing them for future careers in STEM fields while making a meaningful contribution to the advancement of renewable energy.

title: NASA Human Exploration Rover Challenge
text: The NASA Human Exploration Rover Challenge (HERC) is an exciting opportunity for high school students to engage in hands-on STEM learning. By designing, building, and testing human-powered rovers, students develop valuable skills in engineering, problem-solving, and teamwork. The competition fosters creativity and innovation while exposing students to the challenges of space exploration. Participation in HERC also provides networking opportunities with professionals in the field, making it an exceptional platform for students to explore careers in STEM.

title: The Tech Challenge
text: The Tech Challenge is a prestigious competition that empowers high school students to develop their engineering skills and problem-solving abilities. By engaging in a real-world design challenge, participants gain valuable experience in applying the engineering design process, collaborating effectively, and presenting their innovative solutions. The program fosters teamwork, critical thinking, and creativity, while providing a platform for students to showcase their talents and compete for scholarships and recognition.

title: ESTEEM Research Mentoring Program
text: The ESTEEM Research Mentoring Program and the Summer Engineering Research (SER)-Quest is a 4-week research-focused program for rising juniors and seniors in high school. This intensive program is designed to provide students with hands-on research experience in the fields of electrical engineering and mechanical engineering. Students will work closely with faculty mentors and graduate students on real-world research projects. In addition to gaining valuable research experience, students will also develop their teamwork, communication, and problem-solving skills. The program is sponsored by the Center for Minorities in Science and Engineering.

title: HVAC Innovation Challenge
text: SKM's Innovation Challenge is an exciting opportunity for high school students to showcase their creativity and problem-solving skills while gaining valuable experience in the field of engineering. Participants are encouraged to submit papers, ideas, projects, or solutions that demonstrate innovative approaches to industry challenges. The top projects will receive cash prizes of up to $15,000, as well as support for commercializing their projects. This challenge provides a unique platform for students to develop their engineering knowledge, connect with industry professionals, and potentially bring their innovative ideas to life. Apply now and unleash your potential!

title: University of Pennsylvania - Leadership in the Business World
text: University of Pennsylvania's Leadership in the Business World program offers an immersive experience for rising high school seniors. This intensive summer program provides a comprehensive introduction to undergraduate business education at a top-ranked institution. Students engage in hands-on activities, workshops, and discussions, while also honing their leadership, teamwork, and communication skills. Participation in this program empowers students with valuable knowledge and skills that enhance their college applications, prepare them for future leadership roles in business, and foster their personal and professional growth.

title: FBLA
text: FBLA High School is the high school division of Future Business Leaders of America, Inc. (FBLA). It provides high school students with the opportunity to develop their business and leadership skills through academic competitions, leadership development programs, and educational resources. By participating in FBLA, high school students can enhance their knowledge of business principles, develop their public speaking and presentation abilities, and network with other business-minded individuals. FBLA also offers opportunities for students to participate in community service projects and develop their entrepreneurial skills, equipping them with a well-rounded foundation for future success in business and beyond.

title: Youth Citizen Entrepreneurship Competition
text: High school students are encouraged to participate in the Youth Citizen Entrepreneurship Competition, a global initiative empowering young entrepreneurs to address global and community challenges. By submitting innovative ideas and projects that champion the Sustainable Development Goals, students gain a platform to showcase their creativity, problem-solving skills, and commitment to making a positive impact. Participation offers opportunities for mentorship, recognition, and potential funding, fostering the development of entrepreneurial abilities and contributing to a more inclusive and sustainable future.

title: Open Classroom Experience
text: Open Classroom Experience is a 10-week program that will provide high school students with an immersive and hands-on experience in technology, policy, and entrepreneurship. The program will focus on developing students' problem-solving skills, critical thinking skills, and creativity. Through the program, students will have the opportunity to learn from experts in the field, collaborate with peers from around the world, and develop their own innovative solutions to real-world problems. By the end of the program, students will have a better understanding of the current landscape of technology, policy, and entrepreneurship and be equipped with the skills and knowledge necessary to succeed in these fields through college and into their future careers.

title: Technology Student Association
text: The Technology Student Association (TSA) offers high school students a unique opportunity to develop their skills in a variety of technical fields. Through 40 competitions, ranging from computer science to engineering and design, TSA provides a platform for students to showcase their creativity, problem-solving abilities, and leadership potential. Participation in TSA competitions not only enhances students' technical knowledge but also fosters their teamwork, communication, and critical thinking skills. Additionally, TSA offers opportunities for students to connect with industry professionals and gain valuable insights into potential career paths.

title: GATSVI Clubs and Venture Challenge ("GVC")
text: The GATSVI Venture Challenge (GVC) empowers high school students to explore their entrepreneurial potential. Through GVC, students develop business ideas, create startups, and compete for angel and venture capital investments. Participants gain invaluable experience in ideation, market research, financial planning, and pitching, preparing them for future success in business and innovation. Additionally, GVC offers mentorship, networking opportunities, and access to a supportive community, fostering students' entrepreneurial aspirations and equipping them with the skills and confidence to drive positive change in the business world.

title: Stock Pitch Competition
text: This annual flagship event for YIS students is designed to provide hands-on mentoring in financial analysis and hone investment skills. Students individually or in teams of two select a publicly-traded company, analyze it and then present their findings with a "Buy" or "Sell" recommendation to a panel of University Professors and Industry Professionals in the form of a written report and brief. Participating in this competition provides an unparalleled opportunity for students to develop their analytical, presentation, and persuasive speaking skills while gaining valuable insights into the world of finance.

title: Business is Global Summer Language Programs
text: If you are a high school sophomore, junior, or senior, Indiana University's Center for International Business Education and Research offers a two-week summer program that can give you a taste of international business. You will learn about the intersection of business, language, and culture, and you will have the opportunity to practice your language skills in a real-world setting. The program is intensive, but it is also a lot of fun, and it will give you a great foundation for a career in international business.

title: Grammy Camp
text: GRAMMY Camp is an exceptional 5-day summer program designed for high school students passionate about pursuing a career in music. This immersive program offers students the opportunity to explore various career tracks within the music industry, ranging from songwriting and production to music marketing and artist management. Participants gain invaluable insights and mentorship from seasoned music professionals who share their expertise and guide campers towards achieving success in their desired field. The program's focus on practical experience and industry exposure empowers aspiring musicians with the knowledge and skills necessary to navigate the competitive world of music.

title: NYU Music Business Summer Institute
text: Attend a two-week summer institute held at NYU Steinhardt and gain exposure to the current evolving music industry landscape. Learn how to discover, create, market, and distribute music. What is A&R? Artist Branding? By participating in class sessions, going on field trips, attending concerts, and interacting with music industry professionals, you will be given an overview of the current music industry, and be presented with innovative ways to work within it.

title: Wharton Essentials of Entrepreneurship
text: Wharton Essentials of Entrepreneurship immerses high school students in the world of entrepreneurship through a two-week summer program. Students will delve into the creation of new ventures, gaining essential techniques in user research, opportunity testing, MVP development, marketing, scaling, and exiting. Collaborating with peers and engaging in innovative thinking, participants will develop a pitch for an early-stage startup, preparing them for success in the competitive business world.

title: Young Women's Institute
text: The Young Women's Institute (YWI) is a competitive summer program that introduces high school juniors and seniors to the college experience and business career opportunities. Held at Indiana University in Bloomington, Indiana, the program provides selected students from around the country with the opportunity to explore business through interactive workshops, networking opportunities, and industry speakers. YWI is designed to empower young women by equipping them with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to succeed in business and academia.

title: Investment Banking Club: Chapter of the IBC Project
text: The IBC gives high school students the ability to build foundational knowledge of financial markets, learn the fundamentals of investment banking, and create a pathway for their future career.  Participants in this project will gain valuable knowledge in sought after business sectors, insights into a prestigious and rewarding career path, professional and networking opportunities, the chance to gain mentorship, and a furthered, focused understanding of the financial world so as to better inform global decisions in the future.

title: Global Youth Entrepreneur Challenge
text: The Global Youth Entrepreneur Challenge is an annual online competition for high school students to explore their business ideas. The challenge aims to develop young people's confidence and skills through hands-on experience in solving a pressing global problem through entrepreneurship. They learn to grasp science and technology concepts while developing their leadership skills and testing out their business acumen.

title: Innovate WithIN Pitch Competition
text: Innovate WithIN's annual statewide pitch competition empowers high school students from every region of the state to showcase their entrepreneurial ideas. By participating, students not only have the chance to win a $25,000 investment but also gain access to an invaluable network of world-class innovators. This competition provides an exceptional platform for students to bring their business aspirations to life, fostering their entrepreneurial spirit and equipping them with the skills and connections essential for future success.

title: Innovator Competition
text: The Innovator Competition from the Jacobson Institute empowers ambitious high schoolers with a knack for entreprenuership. Participation in this semi-annual event offers students invaluable financial support, allowing them to bring their inventive ideas to life. Seasoned entrepreneurs provide constructive criticism and guidance, fostering the development of critical business acumen. This competition ignites the entrepreneurial spark in young minds, equipping them with the knowledge and resources to shape the future of business innovation.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Challenge
text: The highly competitive Youth Entrepreneurship Challenge invites high school students from all grades to hone their business acumen and entrepreneurial spirit. This eight-month-long series of local, regional, and national business plan and pitch competitions culminates in a high-stakes national championship held in New York City. This provides students with unparalleled opportunities to develop their business ideas, perfect their pitching skills, and receive expert mentorship and feedback. Participation in this prestigious competition not only recognizes students' exceptional ability but also prepares them for success in higher education and the business world.

title: Norm Brodsky Business Concept Competition
text: The Norm Brodsky Business Concept Competition offers an exceptional opportunity for high school students to showcase their entrepreneurial abilities and win a valuable scholarship. By participating, students can develop their business acumen, communication skills, and creativity. The competition fosters a spirit of innovation and provides a platform for students to connect with industry professionals, gaining valuable insights and potential mentorship. The winner of the senior pitch competition is awarded a full tuition scholarship to Rider University, enabling them to pursue their higher education goals and launch their future business endeavors.

title: Berkeley Business Academy For Youth
text: B-BAY (Berkeley Business Academy for Youth) is a summer program for high school students that provides hands-on business and entrepreneurship experience within an immersive learning environment right at the vibrant UC Berkeley campus. Students who attend the program get to learn from knowledgeable professors including PhD candidates and undergraduate youth mentors who are experts in their specialized fields. The program features class projects as well as presentations and is capped off by an end-of-program Demo Day to showcase participants' entrepreneurial talents. B-BAY offers a safe learning environment and all classes are taught in person. All students who are selected to participate will get access to the university's state-of-the-art facilities and resources.

title: International Economics Olympiad
text: The International Economics Olympiad is an annual competition for high school students with a passion for economics, business, and finance. This esteemed competition provides a dynamic platform for students to showcase their problem-solving abilities and deepen their understanding of the complex world of economics. Participation in the Olympiad offers students the opportunity to engage with like-minded peers, foster critical thinking skills, and gain invaluable experience that can pave the way for future success in these fields.

title: Big Idea Competition
text: All high school students are welcome to submit their best business ideas to solve real-world problems. The competition encourages students to use technology to address issues in today's news or that affect their community. The "Big Idea" competition, valued at more than $35,000, will provide cash and other resources to the winning team. For more information, visit the Big Idea website.

title: Conrad Spirit of Innovation
text: The Conrad Spirit of Innovation Challenge is a global competition for high school students to develop innovative solutions to real-world problems using science, technology, engineering and math. This competition inspires participants to apply their critical thinking, creativity and communication skills to challenges that have global impact. With expert guidance and resources, students will expand their collaboration and leadership abilities while networking with like-minded individuals. Moreover, this challenge offers a unique opportunity to build personal and professional skills while making a positive contribution to society.

title: Diamond Challenge
text: The Diamond Challenge is an entrepreneurship competition that offers high school students the opportunity to bring their innovative ideas to life. This national competition, open to students from all backgrounds and experience levels, provides a platform for students to develop their entrepreneurial skills, compete for cash prizes totaling $100,000, and gain access to invaluable resources to support their entrepreneurial journeys. The Diamond Challenge is not just about winning; it's about empowering students to become creative problem-solvers, learn essential business principles, and make a positive impact in their communities.

title: Blue Ocean Competition
text: The Blue Ocean Student Entrepreneur Competition is an action-packed virtual event for ambitious high school-aged entrepreneurs. Participants pitch their innovative business concepts to a panel of experienced entrepreneurs, compete for thousands of dollars in cash prizes, rub shoulders with like-minded individuals from around the world, and receive valuable feedback on their ideas. This competition is an excellent platform for young entrepreneurs to test drive their business concepts in a supportive environment, hone their pitching skills, and take home real-world insights and connections that will propel their entrepreneurial journeys.

title: Bizworld Young Entrepreneur Success!
text: BizWorld's Young Entrepreneur Success! program is a 12-week journey designed to empower aspiring high school entrepreneurs to launch and grow successful businesses. The program offers a dynamic platform featuring guidance from industry experts, virtual networking opportunities with peers, and access to one-on-one mentorship. Through this comprehensive support system, participants can refine their business ideas, gain essential entrepreneurial knowledge, and establish a strong foundation for their business ventures. The program culminates in a live pitch event, where top businesses compete for seed funding of up to $30,000.

title: DECA Competitive Events
text: DECA's competitive events provide high school students with invaluable opportunities to enhance their knowledge and skills in marketing, business, finance, and hospitality. By participating in both written and interactive components judged by industry professionals, students gain practical experience, develop critical thinking abilities, and sharpen their communication skills. DECA's events align with National Curriculum Standards, ensuring students are prepared for college and careers in these highly competitive fields.

title: FCCLA Knowledge Matters Virtual Business Challenge
text: High school students can enhance their financial literacy and business acumen through the FCCLA/Knowledge Matters Virtual Business Challenges. This free competition offers two rounds, focusing on personal finance and fashion management. By participating, students utilize a virtual business simulation to test their decision-making skills, gaining invaluable experience in managing real-world financial and business scenarios. The FCCLA/Knowledge Matters VBC Guidelines provide details on the competition and are accessible via the FCCLA Portal.

title: Project Echo’s High School Business Plan Competition
text: Project ECHO’s High School Business Plan Competition offers an immersive experience for students to hone their entrepreneurial skills and gain valuable feedback from industry professionals. Through the competition, students collaborate in teams to develop comprehensive business plans that outline their innovative start-up concepts. By presenting their ideas to a panel of judges, students refine their communication and presentation abilities, while also receiving expert feedback on the feasibility and potential of their ventures. Participation in this competition fosters entrepreneurial thinking, encourages risk-taking, and prepares students for future success in the business world.

title: tecBridge High School Business Plan Competition
text: The tecBridge High School Business Plan Competition offers an unparalleled opportunity for high school and home school teams to enhance their entrepreneurial skills and prepare for success in the business world. Participants engage in comprehensive research and develop a comprehensive business plan that encompasses market analysis, financial projections, and innovative solutions. Through the competition, students cultivate their critical thinking, problem-solving abilities, and teamwork skills. The competition also provides valuable feedback and mentorship from industry professionals, helping students refine their business ideas and develop valuable connections. By engaging in the tecBridge High School Business Plan Competition, students gain a competitive edge in the marketplace and set a strong foundation for their future business endeavors.

title: Young Entrepreneurs Academy
text: Young Entrepreneurs Academy (YEA!) is an after-school program that transforms high school students into real, confident entrepreneurs. This year-long program provides resources to students in grades 9-12 to research, generate business ideas, write business plans, and launch their own company, with support and mentorship from experienced business professionals. The program culminates in a business plan competition where students pitch their ideas to a panel of investors for a chance to win funding and support for their business ventures.

title: Economics for Leaders (EFL)
text: Economics for Leaders (EFL) is an enriching summer program designed for high school sophomores, juniors, and seniors. Through interactive learning and hands-on activities within a collaborative environment, EFL equips student leaders with the knowledge and skills to incorporate economic principles into their decision-making processes. By understanding economic concepts and their real-world implications, participants develop a deeper understanding of contemporary issues, empowering them to make informed choices and drive positive change.

title: Wharton Global High School Investment Competition
text: The Wharton Global High School Investment Competition offers high school students an unparalleled opportunity to enhance their financial literacy and investment knowledge. By participating in teams, students develop teamwork and communication skills while learning essential concepts such as risk management, portfolio diversification, and industry analysis. The competition provides a challenging and engaging platform for students to apply their knowledge and compete on a global stage, fostering their passion for economics and finance.

title: World Economics Cup
text: World Economics Cup (WEC) is an international education initiative and platform for high school students who are interested in economics. WEC's mission is to identify, inspire, empower and support the next generation of leaders in the economics field and to develop their international network. By participating in this competition, students develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills, engage with leading experts in the economics field, and get a chance to represent their country at the global Finals.

title: The National Economics Challenge
text: The National Economics Challenge (NEC) is an enriching opportunity for high school students with a passion for economics. This prestigious competition allows students to showcase their understanding of micro and macroeconomics, as well as their knowledge of the global economy. Through participation in the NEC, students gain invaluable experience in critical thinking, problem-solving, and presentation skills. Furthermore, they have the chance to connect with like-minded peers, earn recognition, and potentially access scholarship opportunities. The NEC not only fosters a love for economics but also prepares students for success in higher education and beyond.

title: Lights, Camera, Save! Video Contest
text: Lights, Camera, Save! is an annual video contest open to high school students between the ages of 13 and 18 as of February 21, 2022. Students are tasked with creating a 30-second video that educates their peers about the importance of building good financial habits. Students submit their videos to their local bank, which will then select one winner to be entered into a national contest. Four cash prizes are awarded to the national contest winners.

title: Stossel in the Classroom
text: Students in high school can gain recognition for their abilities in economics, film, government, or politics by participating in the Stossel in the Classroom contests. There are divisions for high school students of all ages, ranging from freshmen to seniors. With high cash prizes totaling $25,000 being awarded, students are encouraged to submit their top-notch essays and videos to demonstrate their understanding of these significant subjects.

title: Young Investors Society
text: Young Investors Society (YIS) is a 501(c)3 non-profit organization that provides high school students with investment management experience and leadership opportunities. Taught by experienced investors and university professors, YIS offers interactive learning experiences that equip students with fundamental long-term investing skills. By participating in YIS programs, high school students gain hands-on knowledge, enhance their financial literacy, and build a strong foundation for their future financial success.

title: Wharton Essentials of Finance
text: Wharton Essentials of Finance is a selective summer program for high school students hosted by the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania. This program provides participants with an immersive introduction to the fundamentals of finance, including topics such as financial markets, investment analysis, and portfolio management. Students will gain hands-on experience through case studies, simulations, and guest lectures from industry professionals. Participation in this program not only enhances financial literacy but also develops critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills, making it an invaluable opportunity for aspiring finance professionals or those seeking a competitive edge in college admissions.

title: Technovation Challenge
text: Technovation Challenge empowers high school girls to make a difference by fostering their creativity and technical skills. Through teamwork, mentorship, and hands-on experience, participants develop mobile apps that address real-world problems in their communities. The program enhances problem-solving, leadership, and collaboration while nurturing entrepreneurial and tech acumen – invaluable assets for the future. Additionally, winning teams gain recognition and opportunities to showcase their work on a global platform, empowering them to become confident young leaders in STEM and entrepreneurship.

title: Babson Summer Study
text: Babson Summer Study is a 3+-week experiential online program that can help rising high school juniors and seniors develop an entrepreneurial mindset to become innovators and changemakers. Students can strengthen their understanding of the United Nation's Global Goals, develop the competencies and confidence to address real-world problems, seize opportunities, have an impact, and create change that leads to their desired future. This program is a great way for students to get a head start on their college education while also gaining valuable experience in entrepreneurship, leadership, and teamwork.

title: International Geography Bee
text: The International Geography Bee (IGB) is a globally recognized competition that challenges the geographic knowledge of primary and secondary school students. For high schoolers, participating in IGB offers a unique and enriching experience. Not only does it foster a passion for geography, but it also develops critical thinking, research, and presentation skills. IGB participants have the opportunity to engage with peers from diverse backgrounds, showcase their knowledge, and potentially qualify for the prestigious International Geography Championships, a highly acclaimed event that provides an unparalleled opportunity for geographic exploration and learning.

title: US Geography Championships
text: The United States Geography Championships is a nationwide competition that tests the geography skills of American students. The competition fosters geography education and rewards students who are dedicated to studying the world's countries and peoples. By competing, high school students have the opportunity to become members of the American team at the International Geography Olympiad and gain a deeper understanding of the world.

title: U.S. Department of Energy Student Programs and Internships
text: High School students can gain valuable professional experience through paid internships with the U.S. Department of Energy. These internships provide opportunities to explore future STEM careers, contribute to essential work, and build networks within the federal government. Successful completion could lead to conversion to permanent positions upon graduating. Don't miss this chance to kick-start your career in the exciting field of energy!

title: Constitution Bee
text: The Constitution Bee is a captivating competition that challenges high school students to delve deep into the intricacies of our government and the Constitution. By engaging in this battle of wits, students cultivate essential critical thinking, analytical, and oration skills. Beyond the thrill of competition, the Constitution Bee fosters a profound appreciation for our nation's founding principles, preparing participants to become informed and active citizens in our ever-evolving democratic landscape.

title: National Political Science Bee
text: The National Political Science Bee (NPSB) is a prestigious competition for students in grades 6-12 that tests their knowledge and understanding of political science. High school students who participate in the NPSB benefit from the opportunity to engage with complex political issues, develop their critical thinking skills, and deepen their knowledge of government and political processes. The NPSB has two stages: a Qualifying Exam and the National Championships. Qualifying students compete in state finals and advance to the National Championships to demonstrate their expertise in a rigorous academic environment.

title: United States Senate Youth Program
text: The United States Senate Youth Program (USSYP) is an intensive week-long educational experience and scholarship sponsored by the United States Senate for outstanding high school students who are interested in pursuing careers in public service. The program offers a unique opportunity for students to learn about the Senate, the legislative process, and the role of government in American society. Students will also have the opportunity to meet with Senators, congressional staff members, and other government officials. In addition to the educational experience, the program provides a $10,000 scholarship to each participant.

title: US Senate Page Program
text: The US Senate Page Program grants high school juniors from all 50 states the chance to live and work in Washington D.C. for a semester. Participants not only gain hands-on experience with how the U.S. government functions, but also attend classes in the well-established United States Senate Page School. The school maintains full accreditation by the Middle States Association of Colleges and Schools. Students interested in applying for the Senate Page Program must contact their senator's office to request more information.

title: American Legion Boys State
text: American Legion Boys State is a renowned educational program that provides high school students with hands-on experience in government and leadership. Established in 1935, this selective program consists of mock government simulations where students take on various governmental roles, from local officials to state representatives. Through this dynamic and engaging learning environment, Boys State nurtures critical thinking, public speaking, and leadership skills, preparing students for active and informed citizenship in the years to come.

title: ALA Girls State
text: The American Legion Auxiliary Girls State program empowers high school junior girls with hands-on experience in government and politics. Participants are chosen competitively and engage in a week-long simulation where they learn the intricacies of the political process, elect mock government officials, and actively run a mock government. This immersive experience fosters leadership skills, political awareness, and a deep understanding of the workings of a democratic society, preparing young women to actively participate in civic life.

title: Voice of Democracy
text: The Voice of Democracy audio-essay competition empowers high school students to develop their oratory and critical thinking skills while exploring vital democratic themes. By crafting compelling essays, students enhance their communication abilities, gain a deeper understanding of their civic responsibilities, and potentially earn significant scholarship awards and incentives to support their academic pursuits. With over 25,000 participants annually, this competition provides a platform for students to make their voices heard and contribute to a robust national discourse on democracy and patriotism.

title: Stanford Summer Humanities Institute
text: advertisements.

title: C-SPAN StudentCam
text: High school students passionate about politics should consider submitting an entry for the C-SPAN StudentCam competition, a nationwide video documentary challenge. Participants are encouraged to create a comprehensive video between 5 to 6 minutes that directly addresses how the federal government impacts their lives. Apart from awarding up to 100,000 dollars in prizes, this competition is an exceptional platform for students to showcase their talents in filmmaking, journalism, and political analysis. Moreover, it's an opportunity for them to present their thoughts, perspectives, and solutions regarding the federal government's influence on their lives.

title: Politics For Teens
text: Politics For Teens is a pending 501(c)(4) non-profit organization that aims to advocate for discourse about domestic and global political issues. Their mission is to empower the next generation of leaders in politics and decrease polarization. By participating in competitions, educational meetings, events, media, and voter drives, high school students can learn how to effectively engage in political discussions, develop their leadership skills, and make a difference in their communities.

title: Model UN
text: Are you a high school student eager to develop your public speaking, critical thinking, and negotiation skills? Model UN is the perfect place to showcase your talents. Engage with peers from across the globe, represent countries, and debate real-world issues in a simulated United Nations environment. By participating in this immersive experience, you'll not only gain valuable knowledge about international relations but also boost your confidence, learn diplomacy, and make lifelong connections.

title: Academic WorldQuest
text: Academic WorldQuest, a flagship World Affairs Councils of America youth program, presents a competitive, fast-paced, and spirited event for high schoolers. Encouraging collaborative learning, critical thinking, and teamwork, the program delves into understanding the many dimensions and interconnectedness of world affairs. Participants gain a deeper knowledge of current international politics, geography, and global economics, expanding their perspectives and encouraging informed citizenship.

title: National Current Events League
text: The National Current Events League is an engaging competition that challenges high school students to stay informed about global affairs. Through four meets spread throughout the school year, students tackle 30 multiple choice questions testing their knowledge of recent events. Participation fosters critical thinking, strengthens understanding of world issues, and cultivates a global perspective, making it an invaluable opportunity for students interested in civic engagement and international relations.

title: National Peace Essay Contest
text: The National Peace Essay Contest offers high school students an exceptional platform to develop their critical thinking and writing abilities while gaining an in-depth understanding of peacebuilding and diplomacy. Through participation, students not only engage with foundational concepts but also explore the role of diplomacy in fostering global collaboration and safeguarding national interests.

title: Tufts Summit Program
text: The Tufts Summit program offers a unique opportunity for high school juniors and seniors to delve into International Relations and immerse themselves in French language and culture. Through a college-level course, students explore global affairs while engaging with the vibrant Francophone world. Excursions to Geneva and Lyon provide real-world insights, while extracurricular activities enhance cultural understanding. Participants gain valuable knowledge, international exposure, and language proficiency, preparing them for future academic and professional endeavors. Living with host families fosters cross-cultural exchange, creating lasting friendships and broadening perspectives.

title: American Legion Oratorical Contest
text: This highly esteemed annual competition provides high school students an invaluable opportunity to refine their critical thinking, communication, and leadership skills. Through in-depth study of the U.S. Constitution, participants gain a profound understanding of its principles and the responsibilities of American citizenship. Notable alumni, including Alan Keyes and Lou Dobbs, attest to the impact of the contest on their personal and professional lives.

title: National High School Mock Trial Championship
text: The National High School Mock Trial Championship offers students a unparalleled opportunity to develop essential critical thinking and communication skills through engaging in simulated legal proceedings. The competition challenges students to analyze complex legal issues, research and present evidence, and persuasively argue their cases, fostering a deep understanding of our legal system. Participation in this prestigious tournament not only enhances students' academic performance but also prepares them for future success in law-related fields or any career requiring strong analytical and communication abilities.

title: Virtual Supreme Court
text: The Virtual Supreme Court Competition is an exciting opportunity for high school students to immerse themselves in constitutional law and practice their legal reasoning skills. Teams of two will research and write persuasive appellate briefs on the latest Supreme Court cases, and argue their positions virtually before a panel of esteemed attorneys. Through this competition, students will develop their critical thinking, legal writing, and oral advocacy skills while gaining a deeper understanding of the American legal system.

title: Empire Mock Trial competition
text: The Empire Mock Trial competition provides high school students with an unparalleled opportunity to refine their critical thinking, legal analysis, and communication skills. By competing against top-performing teams on a relevant and complex case, students gain invaluable trial experience that enhances their confidence and prepares them for future legal or debate endeavors. Empire's comprehensive competition experience fosters teamwork, intellectual curiosity, and a deep understanding of the legal system.

title: University of Massachusetts Neuroscience and Mental Health Summer Internship
text: This summer internship is a great opportunity for high school students to dedicate themselves to their chosen field and perfect their skills. Students will learn about the profession that they eventually want to pursue, working hand in hand with professionals and gaining hands on experience in the industry with the top minds. Not only will they be able to learn from the best, they will be exposed to varying aspects of mental health work, giving them a rounded experience no matter where they decide to go after the completion of the internship.

title: TOPSS Competition for High School Psychology Students
text: High school psychology students are invited to participate in the TOPSS Competition, where they can win scholarships of up to $300 for essays that address psychology's role in addressing societal systemic problems. Participation in this competition provides students with an opportunity to develop their critical thinking and writing skills, engage with complex psychological concepts, and demonstrate their passion for psychology. By exploring the intersection of psychology and social issues, students can gain a deeper understanding of the challenges facing society and the potential contributions of psychology to finding solutions.

title: International Psychology Olympiad
text: The International Psychology Olympiad (IPsy) is a prestigious annual competition for high school students with a passion for psychology. The competition fosters the development of critical thinking, problem-solving abilities, and research skills. By participating, students gain invaluable exposure to cutting-edge psychological theories and methodologies, enriching their understanding of the human mind and behavior. The IPsyO competition also provides a platform for students to connect with peers, exchange ideas, and explore potential career paths within the field of psychology.

title: NYU Tisch Summer Program
text: At Tisch Summer High School, cultivate your talents in the performing and cinematic arts and emerging media through rigorous training by our esteemed full-time faculty. Engage in immersive sessions, discover your passion, and prepare for a future in the arts industry. Our programs are highly structured, engaging, and provide an enriching college experience, fostering creativity, self-expression, and collaboration.

title: Congressional Art Competition
text: The Congressional Art Competition is an annual event that gives high school students in every congressional district across the U.S. an opportunity to participate in a unique competition. Many members of the House of Representatives host competitions at the district level for their constituents. Each district's winner will be displayed in the Capitol for a year. The competition is designed to encourage artistic achievement among highschoolers while recognizing the nation's young talent.

title: Cool Science Art Competition on Extreme Weather
text: High school students are invited to participate in the Cool Science Art Competition, expressing scientific concepts through art. Winning artwork will be displayed publicly across multiple states and celebrated at exhibitions. Participants who place will receive monetary rewards and other resources for learning in the arts and sciences. Through this competition, young artists can showcase their talents, foster their interest in science, and inspire the public through their creations, helping to bridge the gap between art and science.

title: Hong Kong Visual Arts Education Festival: International and Local Student Mail Art Competition
text: The International and Local Student Mail Art Competition is a great opportunity for high school students to showcase their creativity and explore the world of Mail Art. The competition is open to students of all ages, and prizes will be awarded to outstanding students in each age group. Participation in the competition not only provides students with an opportunity to have their work recognized, but also to connect with other students from around the world who share their passion for art. Additionally, the competition can help students develop their artistic skills, learn about different cultures, and gain a greater appreciation for the role of art in society.

title: National Poetry Month Poster Contest for Students
text: The National Poetry Month Poster Contest invites high school students to submit their artwork for consideration as the official National Poetry Month poster. The winning student's artwork will be distributed on over 100,000 copies of the poster, which will be displayed in classrooms, libraries, bookstores, community centers, and homes nationwide. Participants have the opportunity to showcase their artistic talents, promote poetry appreciation, and potentially have their work recognized by a national audience.

title: Reflections Arts Program: National PTA
text: The National PTA Reflections Art Program offers high school students an exceptional opportunity to showcase their artistic talents and creativity. With categories ranging from dance choreography to literature, students can explore their unique perspectives and develop their artistic abilities. Participation in this established program fosters confidence, enhances artistic literacy, and instills a lifelong appreciation for the arts. It provides a platform for students to express themselves, connect with peers, and cultivate skills that are essential for academic and personal success.

title: Ocean Awareness Contest
text: By encouraging art and creative communication, the Ocean Awareness Contest offers high school students (ages 11-18) an exciting opportunity to raise awareness for ocean conservation. As young people strive to become leaders in shaping a greener future, this competition allows them to learn about pressing environmental issues affecting our oceans and develop persuasive advocacy for positive change. By sparking passion in young hearts and minds, the Ocean Awareness Contest empowers the next generation of advocates to make a positive impact on the world.

title: Scholastic Art and Writing Awards
text: Participating in the Scholastic Art and Writing Awards offers high school students significant benefits. The competition not only recognizes artistic and literary talent but also provides students with valuable opportunities for professional development. Winners receive recognition through exhibitions, publications, and prestigious scholarships. Additionally, the competition platform allows students to showcase their work to a wider audience, gaining valuable feedback from experts in their fields. By participating, high school students can not only demonstrate their creativity but also expand their portfolios, network with industry professionals, and potentially secure scholarships for higher education.

title: Center for Unsung Heroes ArtEffect Project
text: The Center for Unsung Heroes ArtEffect Project is an inspiring competition giving high school students the opportunity to delve into the lesser-known stories of Unsung Heroes from history and creatively depict them in a visual artwork. By participating, students not only explore diverse perspectives but also hone their research, analytical, and artistic skills. The competition provides a platform to share their artistic interpretations, contribute to historical awareness, and potentially receive recognition for their creative excellence.

title: Doodle for Google
text: Aspiring young artists in grades 9–12 should lend their talents to the Doodle for Google competition where this year's theme is all about inspiration. Students can incorporate the letters G-O-O-G-L-E into their artwork to showcase what sparks their creativity and passions. Participation not only provides a platform for self-expression but also offers substantial rewards. The national winner will be awarded a life-changing $30,000 college scholarship, while their school or non-profit organization will receive an impressive $50,000 technology package. Additionally, the champion will experience an inspiring behind-the-scenes tour with Google's esteemed doodle team. This incredible opportunity empowers high school students to unleash their imagination, refine their artistic abilities, and potentially secure valuable financial support for their future endeavors.

title: Quill and Scroll International Writing, Photo, and Multimedia Contest
text: Calling all high school students! The Quill and Scroll International Writing, Photo, and Multimedia Contest offers an exceptional platform to showcase your skills and creativity. With 23 categories including songwriting, essay writing, and multimedia storytelling, there is an opportunity for every aspiring writer, artist, and photographer. Participants can earn a prestigious National Award Gold Key, receive valuable recognition, and even apply for scholarship opportunities. Don't miss this incredible chance to enhance your artistic abilities, gain recognition for your talents, and potentially secure financial support for your future endeavors.

title: SCAD Rising Star
text: SCAD Rising Star is an immersive summer experience for high school juniors and seniors interested in art and design. Students enroll in one or two college-level classes, building professional portfolios while benefiting from all the perks of being a SCAD student. With access to state-of-the-art facilities and expert faculty, participants gain invaluable college-level experience and a competitive edge in their future art and design endeavors.

title: SCAD Summer Seminars
text: SCAD Summer Seminars not only provide high school students with an immersive and engaging experience in the arts and design but also offer a unique opportunity to develop their skills and explore various artistic disciplines. The seminars, designed for students who have completed their freshman, sophomore, or junior years, foster creativity and provide hands-on experience through interactive art and design projects. These workshops empower students to discover their artistic interests, expand their portfolios, and gain valuable insights into the field of art and design, giving them a competitive edge in their future academic and professional pursuits.

title: California State Summer School for the Arts
text: California State Summer School for the Arts (CSSSA) is a pre-professional training program in visual and performing arts, creative writing, animation, and film for talented high school students. It provides a training ground for future artists wanting to pursue careers in California's arts and entertainment industries.

title: Boston University Visual Arts’ Summer Institute
text: The Boston University Visual Arts’ Summer Institute offers an immersive experience for high school students seeking to advance their artistic skills and prepare for higher education. Through intensive instruction, students gain hands-on experience with materials and techniques used by professionals. This program not only strengthens their portfolios but also provides a glimpse into the academic environment of university-level art education.

title: Synthesis Publications
text: High school students are invited to join Synthesis Publications, an online arts magazine that showcases a wide range of media submissions, from paintings to films to music. As a team member, individuals can develop their artistic skills through publishing their work, lead teams, or manage social media. Participation provides both professional development opportunities and a space for collaboration and personal growth in the arts for all grade levels.

title: Harvard National High School Invitational Forensics Tournament
text: The Harvard National High School Invitational Forensics Tournament is the nation's premier high school debate tournament, offering students unparalleled opportunities to showcase their critical thinking, research, communication, and leadership skills. By participating in Policy Debate, Lincoln-Douglas Debate, Public Forum Debate, Student Congress, and various individual and duo speech events, students gain valuable experience in public speaking, argumentation, and persuasion. This prestigious tournament, held annually on Presidents' Day Weekend in Cambridge, Massachusetts, fosters a competitive and collaborative environment that inspires students to strive for excellence in the art of forensic speech and debate.

title: National Speech and Debate Tournament
text: The esteemed National Speech and Debate Tournament has facilitated oratory excellence since 1931. Each year, thousands of dedicated middle and high school students from across the nation converge at this unparalleled forum to engage in lively debates on contemporary issues, articulately present their perspectives, and share their narratives. Through this rigorous competition, participants develop profound critical thinking, public speaking, and research skills that empower them to become effective communicators and active global citizens. The tournament culminates in a grand finale where champions are celebrated before a captivated live audience and a vast online viewership, solidifying their status as the nation's foremost young orators.

title: Great Communicator Debate Series
text: The Ronald Reagan Great Communicator Debate Series aims to foster the next generation of informed citizen leaders. This nationwide debate competition for high school students emphasizes logic, evidence, and charismatic communication skills. By participating, students can develop their persuasive abilities, enhance their critical thinking skills, and cultivate a deep understanding of important issues. The program honors the legacy of President Ronald Reagan, renowned for his exceptional communication prowess, and empowers students to embrace the civic responsibilities that shape our society.

title: Courageous Persuaders
text: The Courageous Persuaders competition empowers high school students to create impactful 30-second TV commercials addressing critical issues of underage drinking and texting while driving. Through this competition, students gain valuable filmmaking skills, showcase their creativity, and make a tangible difference in raising awareness and shaping behaviors among youth. By participating, students not only contribute to a worthy cause but also enhance their communication, problem-solving, and leadership abilities, while also having the opportunity to earn scholarships and recognition for their efforts.

title: Speak Truth to Power Video Contest
text: The Speak Truth to Power Video Contest encourages high school students to use film as a means to express themselves on human rights issues important to them. This contest is a collaboration between the American Federation of Teachers and the Tribeca Festival and is hosted by Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights. Through the creation of three to five-minute videos in the form of documentaries, narratives, or experimental films, students not only develop a deeper understanding of human rights but also become advocates for change and social justice. The contest is open to students of all backgrounds, and no expensive equipment or prior video editing skills are required to participate. Additionally, this year, there will be special awards given to filmmakers who use only iPhones to create their videos.

title: World of 7 Billion Student Video Contest
text: Calling all high school students! Join the global conversation on population growth by submitting an inspirational video in this international student contest. Showcase your creative problem-solving skills as you propose solutions to the challenges of a growing population, such as food security, environmental preservation, and economic sustainability. Enter today for a chance to win cash prizes, exposure on renowned platforms, and the opportunity to make a real difference on a global scale.

title: Career Safe Youth Safety Video Contest
text: High school students are challenged to create a safety video for the AAA School Safety Video Contest. This competition provides a unique opportunity for students to develop their creativity, problem-solving skills, and public speaking abilities while also promoting safety awareness in their communities. The top three videos will receive awards and be announced at the AAA National School Safety Conference in Washington, D.C.

title: Youngarts' National Arts Competition
text: YoungArts' National Arts Competition offers exceptional benefits to high school students aged 15-18. Through this prestigious program, emerging artists can gain recognition for their talents, receive substantial financial awards of up to $10,000, and access invaluable professional development opportunities led by renowned mentors. Additionally, winners showcase their creations through performances and exhibitions at esteemed cultural institutions, granting them exposure and opportunities to further their artistic journeys. Participation in this renowned competition not only fosters artistic growth but also provides aspiring young artists with the support and platform they need to excel in their chosen field.

title: AASM “Make Sleep Work for You” High School Video Contest
text: High school students in the United States are encouraged to participate in the 2022 AASM "Make Sleep Work for You" High School Video Contest. This contest not only offers cash prizes to the winners but also provides an excellent opportunity for students to raise awareness about the critical importance of sleep for teenagers. By creating original videos between 15 and 90 seconds long, students can demonstrate their understanding of how sleep impacts their physical and mental well-being, academic performance, and overall health. Not only will this contest empower students to become advocates for sleep, but it also allows them to showcase their creativity and storytelling abilities.

title: All-American High School Film Festival (AAHSFF)
text: The All-American High School Film Festival (AAHSFF) is an esteemed competition cultivating the creativity and technical prowess of aspiring high school filmmakers. By showcasing their films on a global stage, students gain invaluable recognition and validation. Participation unlocks access to professional guidance from industry experts, cutting-edge technology demonstrations, and connections with potential mentors. The festival fosters a vibrant community where students collaborate, share ideas, and forge lasting bonds, setting them on a path to future success in the filmmaking realm.

title: ConnectHer Film Festival
text: The ConnectHer Film Festival is an excellent opportunity for high school students to showcase their creativity and storytelling skills while also raising awareness about important women's issues. By submitting an original short film that addresses topics such as gender equality, education, health, and body image, students can make a meaningful impact on the world. Participation in the competition provides a platform for student filmmakers to express their unique perspectives, gain recognition for their work, and contribute to a positive social change.

title: Indy Shorts High School Film Competition
text: Indy Shorts High School Film Competition is a great opportunity for high school students worldwide to showcase their filmmaking talents. Participants compete for the Best Student Film Awards in Narrative, Documentary, Animated, and Indiana Spotlight categories, each offering a $500 cash prize. These category winners then compete for the prestigious $2,000 Summer White Lynch Memorial Award.

title: National Film Festival for Talented Youth
text: The National Film Festival for Talented Youth (NFFTY) is the world's largest film festival for emerging filmmakers in high school. NFFTY celebrates and elevates work by women, BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, and other young persons from traditionally marginalized communities. NFFTY provides high school students with an opportunity to showcase their work, connect with industry professionals, and learn from experienced filmmakers. Participating in NFFTY's competition can help high school students gain recognition for their work, build their portfolios, and prepare for careers in the film industry.

title: FutureWave Shorts Competition
text: Aspiring young filmmakers in high school have the exceptional opportunity to participate in the prestigious FutureWave Shorts Competition at the acclaimed Seattle International Film Festival (SIFF). This esteemed competition showcases original short films crafted by talented filmmakers aged 18 and under, offering a platform for them to share their artistic vision and showcase their exceptional filmmaking abilities. Participation in the FutureWave Shorts Competition provides a wealth of invaluable benefits for high school students, including the potential to receive the coveted Wavemaker Award for Excellence in Youth Filmmaking, fostering their creativity, and honing their technical skills. Furthermore, the competition grants them the opportunity to have their work seen by industry professionals and a diverse audience, potentially opening doors to future opportunities in the field of filmmaking.

title: Austin Film Festival Young Filmmakers Competition
text: High school students have a great opportunity to participate in the Austin Film Festival's Young Filmmakers Competition. To foster the next generation of storytellers, the competition seeks creative and innovative films from young filmmakers in the narrative, animated, and documentary categories. Selected submissions will be showcased on the big screen in front of a supportive Festival audience, allowing young filmmakers to share their artistry with an appreciative crowd. They will also get insights into the film industry, potentially inspiring them to pursue a career in filmmaking or related fields. Participating in the competition can be an enriching and unforgettable experience for budding filmmakers.

title: The 90-Second Newbery Film Festival
text: The 90-Second Newbery Film Festival challenges young filmmakers to distill the essence of Newbery-winning novels into engaging 90-second films. Participation offers high school students unique creative and intellectual opportunities. By adapting beloved stories to the screen, students develop their storytelling abilities, critical thinking skills, and cinematic techniques. Moreover, the competition fosters collaboration, encourages creativity, and provides a platform for aspiring filmmakers to showcase their talents.

title: National Greek Exam
text: The National Greek Exam, hosted by the esteemed American Classical League, presents an exceptional opportunity for high school students to demonstrate their proficiency in Ancient Greek. This prestigious exam encourages students to cultivate an in-depth understanding of the language's nuances and immerse themselves in its rich history and cultural significance. Participation in the National Greek Exam not only tests students' skills but also fosters their appreciation for the language and its enduring influence on Western civilization.

title: National Italian Exam
text: The National Italian Exam (NIE) evaluates high school students' Italian language proficiency through written and aural interpretation assessments. Its rigorous standards align with ACTFL Performance Descriptors and Proficiency Guidelines. Top-performing students earn esteemed prizes, including monetary awards, study trips to Italy, medals, and certificates. Participating in the NIE allows students to showcase their Italian language skills, gain recognition for their achievements, and potentially expand their future opportunities.

title: National Japan Bowl
text: This highly-regarded competition offers participants an opportunity to showcase and expand their Japanese language skills. High school students can benefit greatly from participating in the Japan Bowl by developing confidence in their language abilities, enhancing their understanding of Japanese culture, and broadening their global perspective. The competition encourages teamwork, reinforces critical thinking, and fosters camaraderie among students with shared interests. By immersing themselves in this competitive environment, participants can gain invaluable experience that can serve them well in their future academic and professional endeavors.

title: National Latin Exam
text: The National Latin Exam (NLE) presents a magnificent opportunity for high school Latin students to showcase their skills and earn recognition for their academic achievements. This annual test provides students with an avenue to reinforce their classroom learning while potentially qualifying for scholarships. Participants can strive to achieve certificates, medals, and scholarship opportunities based on their exam performance, making it a valuable addition to any student's academic portfolio.

title: National German Exam
text: The National German Exam offers high school students an unparalleled opportunity to showcase their German language skills and engage in intellectual competition. Administered annually to over 20,000 participants, the Exam empowers students with valuable diagnostic feedback, fostering their progress in language learning. Outstanding performers are recognized through an impressive prize program, instilling a sense of accomplishment and motivation. By providing teachers with comparative data, the Exam aids in curricular development and facilitates the identification of best practices. Participation in the National German Exam empowers students to measure their achievements, develop their German proficiency, and connect with a vibrant community of language enthusiasts.

title: Translators without Borders
text: Translators without Borders offers high school students a unique opportunity to make a meaningful impact through their language skills. By joining the organization as a volunteer, students can utilize their language proficiency to support diverse projects, ranging from medical translations to crisis response efforts. Participating in these projects not only allows students to enhance their language abilities but also fosters a sense of global responsibility, cultural understanding, and empathy.

title: TED Translators
text: TED Translators offers high school students the unique opportunity to contribute to a global community while developing valuable language skills. By volunteering as a translator or transcriber, students can make TED Talks accessible to a wider audience, breaking down language barriers and fostering understanding. Participating in this program not only enhances language proficiency but also develops cultural empathy, critical thinking, and a sense of purpose. It is an exceptional opportunity for students to make a meaningful impact while honing their linguistic abilities and expanding their global perspective.

title: Certamen
text: Certamen is a captivating quiz-bowl style competition for high school students studying Latin, Greek, and classical civilizations. By engaging in this game, students have the chance to showcase their comprehension of ancient languages, cultures, and civilizations, as well as their understanding of the enduring impact these topics have on the contemporary world. Participation in Certamen not only fosters a profound understanding of Classics but also sharpens critical thinking, research, and teamwork skills, making it an invaluable asset for students seeking academic excellence and personal growth.

title: US History Bee
text: The US History Bee is a prestigious competition that challenges high school students to delve deeply into American history. By participating, students not only enhance their knowledge of their nation's past but also develop critical thinking, analytical, and problem-solving skills. The competition provides a platform for students to showcase their understanding of historical events, figures, and concepts, fostering a passion for learning and an appreciation for their country's heritage.

title: Citizen Archivist
text: Become a Citizen Archivist and contribute to preserving our country's past while developing valuable skills. Join the National Archives' initiative where students engage in transcribing, tagging, and commenting on historical documents. Through this virtual opportunity, you'll actively support the accessibility and searchability of these records. Participation offers not only a firsthand experience in history but also enhances your research, critical thinking, and communication abilities.

title: By The People Virtual Volunteer
text: By the People is a virtual volunteer opportunity for students to transcribe and review historical documents from the Library of Congress. By participating, students can not only gain valuable experience in history, but also contribute to the preservation and accessibility of American heritage. The program is open to students of all grades and provides a meaningful way to engage with the nation's history while fostering digital literacy skills.
